Read CLAUDE.md, then STATUS.md, then rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md. Start from a fresh main.

Task: build BRIEF-gui.md, in the three pull requests its "Order of work" gives:
  A. Page organisation (sections 1–4). Page only; no engine change.
  B. The four new powers (section 5). Engine and page.
  C. More points of comparison for energy (section 6). Research first.
All the canon the brief relies on is confirmed and recorded in CLAUDE.md; nothing in it waits on a decision.

How to work:
- Claim rex-strength-lab/ in STATUS.md (and any other files you'll touch), on your own claude/... branch. Release the claim when you finish.
- Follow the house pattern in CLAUDE.md: every number sourced or labelled an estimate; tests for each change; the full Rex lab build line from CLAUDE.md passing; README and known limits updated; adversarial review rounds with every finding reproduced in code before it counts, and the records in rex-strength-lab/research/reviews/.
- Keep to the brief's rules: in A the engine is untouched and every existing test passes unchanged. In B, with all four powers off (5a at 0%), every engine result matches today's exactly (calibration, presence, the all-out baseline, the sweep). Saved pages still load, with retired settings migrated as each section says.
- Section 6 needs the full research process (a researcher, then a skeptic who fetches every source), run the way the presence research was (history/scratchpad/workflows/). The candidate references in the brief are unverified starting points.
- Where the brief is unclear, or the code doesn't match what it describes, check the code, decide, and note the decision in the pull request. Ask me only about canon.
- One pull request at a time. Open A when it's done and tested, then stop and tell me. I'll merge it and tell you to start B. Then the same for C. Let CI finish before I merge.
- After each merge, rebuild and republish the live Rex lab page to its existing URL (listed in the root README).
- Update STATUS.md before every push. This is a long run, so finish with a history/ entry built the same way as the existing ones.
I'll start from a fresh main and read the three files.

The ENGINE (src/engine.js) MUST BE UNCHANGED and every existing test must pass unchanged.
See the diff: git -C /home/user/rex-strength-lab diff main...claude/rex-gui-a (main's page build is git show main:rex-strength-lab/dist/index.html). Code: src/app.html (search BAY, renderInto, renderSolo, renderDuo, scheduleDuo, stopDuo, duoMode, isDuo, duoCap, pickTab, buildTabs, makeDuoPlan/harmAt, stepDuoPlan, resolveDuoEffort, renderDial, buildControls, the state migration near 'Retired settings'), src/static-data.js, build-data.py, research/final-duo.json, README.md, test/shots.js, test/make-page-fixture.js, test/fixtures/page-before.json.
Build: cd /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab && python3 build-data.py && node build.js. Tests: node test/calibration.js (80 s), node test/presence.js (60 s), node test/shots.js (2 min; writes dist/preview.html and shots/). Render pages yourself with Playwright: require('/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright'); chromium.launch({ executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome' }); wrap dist/index.html in '<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"></head><body>' + html + '</body></html>' and load it from a file URL under your scratch folder (do the same with main's build for comparisons). The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first (see CLAUDE.md). Do NOT edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab and do not commit; work on copies. Write scratch scripts and screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewA1/ (create it; use a subfolder named for your lens). Every finding must be reproduced: give the exact input or place, what the page or code does (quote it, or the script output), what is correct and why, and a minimal fix. Report real defects only: behaviour the brief requires that is missing or wrong, results that changed when they must not, wrong or unsupported claims, contradictions, broken layout or controls, accessibility failures, bugs in state handling or background work, tests that don't test what they say. Skip style preferences.

Another reviewer (code lens) reported the findings below. For EACH one, try hard to REFUTE it: reproduce it yourself with your own script or browser run, independently of theirs (write it under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewA1/verify-code/). A climb past 150 km jumps along an exact Kepler arc (`conicTo`). If Cd is not above 0, the whole flight is that arc, so vacuum is exact. The step is 0.002·v/a, capped. Outputs include range, apex, vImpact, maxMach, maxStagT (an equilibrium-air table), eFold = 2m/(ρ₀·Cd·A) and the path. (a) Nothing breaks: no sinking, hole, crater, punch-through or fall into the planet.
(b) It supplies bearing. anchorCapacity sets Nmax = Infinity. jumpOnce sets RB = Infinity and cB = 0, so the feet never move. sprint sets stanceCap = Infinity. COLLIDE.holdOf gives a vertical hold of H = Infinity. So the move gets its full push.

So in mechanics, 5c is groundHolds renamed. It is not in prints, in the table, in labels, or in the 'break the ground' preset.

HOW SHAKING IS COMPUTED. Ground shaking is momentum (impulse) based and never reads groundHolds.
- vibSource and impulseSource: a Hann pulse with peak F = 2J/T, or a ramp.
- ppvElastic: near = 0.375 F/(ρ cs² T r), far = 0.620 F/(ρ cs^2.5 T^1.5 √r), times the damping D(ξr/(0.919 cs T)). Past 60 m it falls no faster than r^-1.3.
- Ground values come from VIB.GROUND per surface. Ice and steel have no entry, so their ppv is 0 with the power on or off.
- plasterLimit is the USBM RI 8507 Fig. B-1 curve at f = 1/T. Rattle is 1 mm/s. A stomp's feelOnce is 1.0 mm/s.

The sources, move by move:
- Walk: walkStep src = [Hann Fpulse over Tpulse (heel strike), ramp kLoad·W over tRamp].
- Stomp: MOVES.stomp.shake has J = p(vFoot, legEff) + max(0, stampMass − legEff)·min(vFoot, stampSpeed) and T = max(footPulse, 2·holeDepth/vFoot), with footPulse = 0.052·√(0.45H/0.9) s.
- Jump: MOVES.jump.shake is the landing only, [p(vLand, m) over 2d/vLand, plus 2·legEff·vLand over footPulse unless Soft landing is on]. The take-off push is not a source in either mode.
- Throw: MOVES.throw.shake is the object's momentum over max(1 ms, L/vImpact), where it lands. The thrower's push into the ground is not counted.
- Punch, clap, sprint and pull have no shake (the page shows NO_SHAKE). Lift and Weight are static.
- Separately, seismicMagnitude(E) = (log10(1e-4·E) − 4.8)/1.5 is energy based. Stomp uses E (not gated). Throw uses Eimpact (not gated). Jump uses Eground (gated). Arm pin uses push E (not gated). Collide uses Q when held. instantGrowth uses Eground (gated).

How the solo tabs judge shaking. Each solo move's RESTRAINT.MOVES[m].shake(r, o) (engine 3132-3226) turns a push into the ground into a source. The usual form is impulseSource(surface, J, T) (2889): a Hann pulse that peaks at 2J/T and lasts T. It is not exported. Throw landing: J = m·v_impact over max(1 ms, L/v). Jump: the body's m·v over the landing stroke L.t, plus the feet's 2·legEff·v over footPulse (64 ms at 10 ft). Stomp: (legEff + stamp mass)·v over max(footPulse, 2·holeDepth/vFoot). Punch, clap, sprint and pull have no source. ppvAt (2890) is the Lamb vertical point-load model (near field 1/r, Rayleigh 1/√r, damping; no faster than r^-1.3 past 60 m). plasterOver and plasterReach (2928-2929) compare it with USBM RI 8507 Fig. B-1 at 1/T: 12.7 mm/s from 2.7 to 10 Hz, 36.8 mm/s at a 35 ms pulse. HAZARDS 'plaster' and PRESETS 'rattle' (≥1 mm/s at near, or blast ≥36 Pa at near) and 'plaster' use these (3227-3245). The page's planFor calls RESTRAINT.plan, one resumable log-grid search per job ('goal', 'hazard:x', 'preset:x'), with runs memoised per effort. resolveEffort runs only the selected preset's job, and never goes below least disruptive.

Two-player tests today. duoHarm(act) (app 3382) returns the first harm as a string, or null. makeDuoPlan (3479) runs one RESTRAINT.search on !!harm, from lo = 1.2·m·g/1.4 (2,577 kgf at canon) to the dial, at 5% tolerance. Saturation uses the duoSig fingerprint. The only efforts offered are least, all-out and custom.
- Arm: table torn, slam > table, pin crater, pin 'quake' > 2, fireball.
- Wrestle: shove (supersonic, or a slide past near); throw (boom, landing blast, landing plaster, ground, recoil slide). Shoving match and lift: null.
- Catch: recoil slide, supersonic, object destroyed, grip crush, passenger. The partner toss: null.
- Collide: push reading null; charge: boom, blast (unless a thump), slide.

No two-player test has a shaking source. None returns the momentum the ground takes, except collide's h.inel.pT and h.el.pT (the Earth's share when held), partial.Jearth = H·τ, and quakeHeld = seismicMagnitude(Q). quakeHeld assumes all of Q reaches the ground at 1e-4 seismic efficiency. Computed (canon bodies, 100 t dial, concrete, comic, near 5 m):
- Ollie sprints (18.1 m/s) into a bolted Rex. The ground takes J = p = 5.46e4 N·s over T = 34.7 ms. That is 64.5 mm/s at 5 m (plaster may crack out to 12.0 m, rattle to 227 m, felt to 574 m), past the elastic strain limit inside about 12-30 m. quakeHeld says magnitude -2.07, shown as 'No noticeable quake'. For scale, an all-out solo stomp at the same strength gives 3.3 mm/s at 5 m.
- A bounce sends 2p over the spring time: 42.8 mm/s.
- With a standing Rex the hit is not held. Only Jearth = 615 N·s goes into the ground during the hit: 0.73 mm/s. The rest leaves over the 7 m slide, as friction about the size of their weight.
- Jump onto Rex (held by bearing, or always held with 5c on): 4.98e4 N·s over 38 ms, 47 mm/s.
- Bolted holder: the plaster onset is about 8 t of effort (8.8%), the same with comic ground on or off. Jump onto him: 70.6 t (78%). A standing holder never reaches plaster.
- Other tests: a bolted Ollie shoved at 1e6 t gets 6.8e6 N·s in 2 ms (plaster out to 1.1 km). A static bolted push (8.9e5 N, ramp τ = 0.188 s) gives 1.42 mm/s. A caught car (30 m, easy) gives 1.32 mm/s. Wrestle's thrower's feet at 100 t: 1.16 mm/s, versus 7.48 mm/s from the landing.

Every push move runs through `pushApart({F, d, mA, mB, RA, RB})`: an internal force F pushes Rex's body (mA, his mass less the hand or arm that moves with the load) and the load (mB) apart over a stroke d.
- A side moves only once F beats its hold R.
- Comic mode: constant net force, relativistic, with p = (F − R)t. Real mode integrates Hill's curve.

Rex's hold comes from `anchorCapacity` (line 331):
- Friction: R = min(R1, R2), where R1 = [μ(mA g + mB g cos²θ) + mB g sinθ cosθ] / (cosθ − μ sinθ) and R2 = μ·Nmax/cosθ + mB g sinθ, with Nmax = bearing × 2 feet.
- Once he slips: Rslide(F) = F − cosθ·max(0, F cosθ − mB g sinθ cosθ − μ·min(N(F), Nmax)).
- `'bolted'`: R = Rslide = ∞. N and Nmax are still returned, so bearing and sinking are still judged.

With a finite R the stroke is shared: his body lurches back push.xA during the push.

Per move:
- **Throw** (`throwOnce`): his recoil momentum after the follow-through is pA − pB·armMass/mB, because the arm stops inside him; recoilV and recoilE follow from it. If F > R he also tries pushing only to R (heldBack) and keeps the faster throw.
- **Punch**: RA = anc.R (static). recoilV = vA, lurch = xA.
- **Clap**: RA is already ∞. The two hands push off his chest equally and opposite, so there is no recoil.
- **Pull**: modelled as a walk with the load. usable = min(drive, anc.R), a = (usable − resist)/(m_obj + m_body).
- **Stomp**: RA = mA g, or ∞ when bolted. The reaction launches his body (vBody).
- **Sprint**: bolted removes the μN and soft-ground caps on thrust.

Bolted sends recoil into the planet only implicitly: pA = 0, xA = 0, and the load gets the whole stroke. No result records the momentum the ground took, and no tab turns it into ground shaking. RESTRAINT's shake sources are only landings, stomps and jumps.

- `'slide'`: `MOVES.throw.slide = recoilSlide = push.xA + coastDist(m, recoilV·cosθ, R, ½ρ Cd A) ≥ near`. It is 0 when bolted.
- `'boom'`: boomSpeed counts recoilV.
- `'air'`: throwBlast's path adds recoilE past Mach 1.
- In the two-player tests, Catch counts the thrower's coast (`recoilOf`), and the page's `duoHarm` counts the slides from the Wrestle throw and the shove.

ownRecoil is a ctx flag, consumed per move. Do not rewrite ctx.anchor, or sprint and the being-pushed paths would change.

For his own push on something else it is exactly `'bolted'` footing for that stroke: `ownAnchor(c) = c.ownRecoil ? 'bolted' : c.anchor` in throwOnce, punchOnce, recoilOf and shoveOnce's pusher. The stomp is a question (below). It is more than "stop the slide": with R = ∞ his body never moves during the stroke, so the whole stroke goes into the load and he never holds back.

This is what "as if bolted" means physically, and it raises results:

text:
B's engine and page work is finished and pushed to `claude/rex-gui-b` (not yet a pull request). The full Rex lab test line passes, including the new `node test/powers.js` (51/51). Review round 1 is running now, and I'll pick up from its results when it reports.

What's in the branch:
- **Powers off still matches `main`.** With all four powers off, 14,883 engine results match `main` exactly. The page's saved-state comparisons with `main` also still match.
- **Their powers panel:** the four default powers replace Comic ground, Gentle hold and Cool flight. Old saves load with all four on. The Air resistance absorbed slider shows a percentage and what that setting means. No preset ever moves it.
- **Ground shaking:** with Unbreakable footing or They take their own recoil on, the push that goes through their feet into the ground now shakes it. This shows on the solo moves, the Arm wrestle pin, the shove, the throws in Wrestle and Catch, and the Collide hit. The shaking also counts in the courtesy-ceiling checks.
- **Two-player presets:** all four two-player tests now offer the six not-so-heroic presets. On Collide with Rex bolted, "risk cracking the plaster" finds an effort (9% of their strength). With Rex just standing, it says the hit never does: his feet slide, so the ground only takes his friction.
- **Very fast throws** now fly in a straight line. The All-Star baseball at 100% leaves the Earth with no fireball.
- **The lower-the-slider hint** shows when an air preset is out of reach only because of the slider. It shows for a level baseball at 10⁶ t and not at 10⁴ t.
- **Break the ground** sets Unbreakable footing aside for that preset only.
- The assumption cards and the README's Known limits are updated.

Three places where my results differ from what the brief expects:
- **50% air on the All-Star baseball:** the fireball carries about 74% of the energy at 0%, not half. The relativistic model behind it doesn't scale in a straight line.
- **"Any effort set past" break the ground:** I didn't make that turn the power off. All-out is past it, so every all-out result would break the ground.
- **Collide into an "immovable object":** I tested this with Rex bolted. The infinite-mass thought experiment needs no ground, so nothing reaches the ground there.

One canon question for you, which will go in the PR: with Unbreakable footing on, instant growth can't drive Rex's soles into the ground. For now he grows upward from them, as he did on Comic ground. Is that right, or should Unbreakable footing step aside while he grows?

I also added `node test/powers.js` to the build line in `CLAUDE.md` and to CI, one line each; I added both files to my claim in `STATUS.md`. These will be in the PR notes.

Next: fix whatever the skeptics confirm, run more review rounds until they come back clean, then open PR B and stop.

10. The ocean figures are the drag the air would have taken along the path actually flown.
11. Not modelled: Everest hitting a bird / the Moon (no thrown-object collisions besides the landing); ice and a steel deck have no ground-wave model.

14. The lower-the-slider hint shows only on Throw and Catch, only for the air presets, only when the same search at 0% finds an effort.
15. Old saves pick up all four on, even a saved Comic ground or Gentle hold that was off.
16. CLAUDE.md's build line and CI gained node test/powers.js.
17. Canon question for the owner: with Unbreakable footing on, instant growth can't drive his soles into the ground, so he grows upward from them (as on Comic ground).

1. Every new behaviour is gated by its power; with all four off the engine equals main (powers-off fingerprint) and the page's saved-state comparisons run with the powers off. New result fields appear only when a power is on.
2. 'Break the ground' sets Unbreakable footing aside for that preset only (its search, effort, courtesy ceiling and the tab shown run on real ground). Not for a custom effort past it: all-out is past it, so every all-out result would break the ground, and the ceiling (worked out with the power on) could sit past the break. The two-player 'ground' preset does the same.
3. The arm-wrestle table counts as a held thing (Things keep their form holds it).
4. They take their own recoil covers his throw, punch, stomp (not Collide's stomp-launch), a pull (only the rope's pull back goes into the planet; his legs still need friction), a shove, the thrower in Catch and Wrestle; not arm wrestling, the push match or Collide (Bolted is for being pushed). A clap has no net recoil.
5. At 100% absorbed his hand still breaks the sound barrier (their own bodies meet real air), so the boom hazard stays; only the object's flight stops booming.
6. The near-field blast from a throw is (1 - share) x the drag loss of the slowed flight; the slowed flight's whole energy balance gives the air nearly the full drag loss at 50%, spread over a longer path; we judge the blast near him.
7. Throws past 1% of light speed use the game of catch's relativistic snowplow, which is not linear in the share: at 50% the All-Star baseball's fireball carries about 74% of the 0% value, not half.
8. The Throw tab's relativistic text was wrong at high gamma (it put all the energy into a fireball within tens of metres; the engine's own snowplow gives about 25% over the whole level path for the All-Star ball) and is gamma-corrected.
9. Energy taken back from the air stays with the object; it doesn't feed growth.
10. The ocean figures are the drag the air would have taken along the path actually flown.
11. Not modelled: Everest hitting a bird / the Moon (no thrown-object collisions besides the landing); ice and a steel deck have no ground-wave model.
12. 'The Collide charge into an immovable object shakes the ground' is tested with Rex bolted (the page's immovable object); the infinite-mass thought experiment needs no ground; standing Rex slides, the ground takes only his friction, and the plaster preset says it never does.
13. Two-player ground shaking only with the powers on (toGround only then, to keep powers-off results identical); with them off the presets say the shaking isn't modelled; a thrown partner's landing stays a source as before.
14. The lower-the-slider hint shows only on Throw and Catch, only for the air presets, only when the same search at 0% finds an effort.
15. Old saves pick up all four on, even a saved Comic ground or Gentle hold that was off.
16. CLAUDE.md's build line and CI gained node test/powers.js.
17. Canon question for the owner: with Unbreakable footing on, instant growth can't drive his soles into the ground, so he grows upward from them (as on Comic ground).
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first (see CLAUDE.md). Do NOT edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab and do not commit; work on copies. Write scratch scripts and screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewB1/ (create it; use a subfolder named for your lens). Every finding must be reproduced: give the exact input or place, what the page or code does (quote it, or the script output), what is correct and why (with numbers), and a minimal fix. Report real defects only: wrong physics or formulas, momentum or energy bookkeeping errors, behaviour the brief requires that is missing or wrong, results that changed when the powers are off, wrong or unsupported claims, contradictions between page text and engine numbers, broken layout or controls, accessibility failures, bugs in state handling or background searches, tests that don't test what they say. Skip style preferences.

LENS: COPY, CLAIMS AND LAYOUT. Render the page (390x844 and 1280x900, light and dark) and read every new or changed sentence, label, chip, tile, hint and summary: Their powers panel (the four powers, the slider #air-absorb with #air-absorb-big and #air-absorb-read at 0, 30, 50, 100%, the hints), #powers-sum in many states, every tab's verdicts, chips, tiles, 'what happens' items and math lines with the powers on and off (Throw at gentle, all-out, supersonic, relativistic and the All-Star baseball at 0, 50, 100%; Lift; Jump; Stomp; Punch; Sprint; Pull; Weight; Walk; Arm wrestle; Wrestle push, shove, throw; Catch with each object and a partner; Collide charge and push, bolted and standing), the effort readouts (offBy lines, the break-the-ground note, the lower-the-slider hint, the two-player presets' texts including 'not modelled' notes), the assumption cards (static-data.js), README.md (Known limits and the test descriptions) and research/final-environment.json's new facts. Check each claim against the engine numbers: is it true, specific and not misleading? Are there leftover references to Comic ground, Gentle hold or Cool flight, or text that is now wrong with the powers on (e.g. 'the ground under him turns to plasma' with Unbreakable footing, 'he gets shoved back' with own recoil, 'drag slows it' at 100%)? Is each power labelled where it changed a result? Also layout and accessibility of the new controls: the slider's label and aria-valuetext, focus order, contrast, overflow, the new chips at 390 px. House rules: plain, short sentences; gloss jargon; plain numbers. Report only real defects.

Under verified_ok, list what you checked and found correct. Prefix finding ids with "copy-".

2. 'Break the ground' sets Unbreakable footing aside for that preset only (its search, effort, courtesy ceiling and the tab shown run on real ground). Not for a custom effort past it: all-out is past it, so every all-out result would break the ground, and the ceiling (worked out with the power on) could sit past the break. The two-player 'ground' preset does the same, with its own real-ground ceiling.
3. The arm-wrestle table counts as a held thing (Things keep their form holds it).
4. They take their own recoil covers his throw, punch, stomp (not Collide's stomp-launch), a pull (only the rope's pull back; his legs still need friction), a shove, the thrower in Catch and Wrestle; not arm wrestling, the push match or Collide. A clap has no net recoil.
5. At 100% absorbed his hand still breaks the sound barrier (their own bodies meet real air), so the boom hazard stays; past 1% of light speed his hand's own air also makes a fireball (handAir, an upper bound), counted below 100% too (at 0% main's count, all of the object's energy, is kept).
6. The game of catch's blast uses the same rule.
7. Past 1% of light speed both tabs use a relativistic snowplow in which the object sweeps air at the share of the rate. In the ground's frame the air takes E(1 - keep). Close to light speed a small share of a long column still takes almost all the energy: for the All-Star baseball (about 10,000 of its own masses of air on a level path) 50% gives over 99.9% of the 0% value, not the half the brief's test expects; the brief's 'half' holds only for something that sweeps little air (the Great Pyramid just past 1% of light speed: about 51%).

9. Energy taken back from the air stays with the object; it doesn't feed growth.
10. The ocean figures are the drag the air would have taken along the path actually flown.
11. Not modelled: Everest hitting a bird / the Moon (no thrown-object collisions besides the landing); ice and a steel deck have no ground-wave model (the page says so).

Review round 1 is done and its fixes are pushed to `claude/rex-gui-b`; round 2 is now running in the background. There's no pull request yet.

**Round 1 result:** 52 findings, and the skeptics confirmed all 52. I fixed 51. The one left is a recorded decision: with Unbreakable footing and They take their own recoil both off, a throw's push into the ground still isn't counted as shaking, because the powers-off results have to match `main`. The README's Known limits now says so.

**Fixes that change what the page tells you:**
- **The 50% air test still fails.** I had calculated the air's share of a very fast throw wrongly. Corrected, the All-Star baseball at 50% loses more than 99.9% of the 0% fireball energy to the air, not half. It meets about 10,000 times its own mass of air, so even half the drag takes almost everything. "Half at 50%" only holds for something that sweeps little air, such as the Great Pyramid just past 1% of light speed (about 51%).
- **Throw tab text at 0% matches `main` again** (with Things keep their form off).
- **His hand now counts too.** Past 1% of light speed his throwing hand meets real air, so it makes its own fireball, given as an upper bound.
- **Game of catch at 100%:** a throw that fast flies in a straight line. Past about 12 km that line runs underground, so it hits the ground instead of reaching Ollie. A catch at that speed now conserves momentum, and Ollie gets carried off. Before, the engine reported him sliding 20 km at 48 times light speed.
- **Stomp:** Unbreakable footing now only steps in where real ground would actually break. Dents and footprints stay.
- **Collide:** the stomp-launch charge works again; They take their own recoil had been blocking it.
- **Other fixes:** text that credited a power where it changed nothing, the ice and steel deck shaking claims, the two-player break-the-ground preset (now on real ground), and the missing courtesy-ceiling line in the two-player effort box.

**Tests:** calibration, presence, the page tests and `test/powers.js` (65 checks) all pass on the branch. With the powers off, the engine matches `main` in all 14,936 cases. That set now includes the code paths the reviewers said it missed, and I regenerated it from `main`'s engine.

**Still open for you:** the canon question about instant growth with Unbreakable footing, plus the decisions above. Both go in the PR.

Next: fix whatever round 2 confirms, update the README review history, open PR B, and stop for you.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary request and intent

The user (the owner, working in cloud sessions) asked for `rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md` to be built as three pull requests, one at a time:

- **A.** Page organisation (sections 1–4). Merged as #20 and live as version 11.
- **B.** The four new default powers (section 5). This is in progress now.
- **C.** Energy comparisons (section 6). Research comes first: a researcher, then a skeptic who fetches every source.

Rules from the original message, preserved:
- "Claim rex-strength-lab/ in STATUS.md (and any other files you'll touch), on your own claude/... branch. Release the claim when you finish."
- Follow the house pattern:
  - every number sourced or labelled an estimate;
  - tests for each change;
  - the full Rex lab build line passing;
  - README and known limits updated;
  - adversarial review rounds with every finding reproduced in code, and records in rex-strength-lab/research/reviews/.
- "Saved pages still load, with retired settings migrated as each section says."
- "Where the brief is unclear, or the code doesn't match what it describes, check the code, decide, and note the decision in the pull request. Ask me only about canon."
- "One pull request at a time. Open A when it's done and tested, then stop and tell me. I'll merge it and tell you to start B. Then the same for C. Let CI finish before I merge."
- "After each merge, rebuild and republish the live Rex lab page to its existing URL." That URL is https://claude.ai/artifact/YFpbHtX8tM2Qwffd6znbZP.
- "Update STATUS.md before every push. This is a long run, so finish with a history/ entry built the same way as the existing ones."
- With all four powers off (5a at 0%), every engine result must equal main's.

Conventions:
- Commit messages end with:
  ```
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Uj6G3iasxRWVsuqr1BAzrS
  ```
- PR bodies end with:
  ```
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

  https://claude.ai/code/session_01Uj6G3iasxRWVsuqr1BAzrS
  ```
- No model IDs in commits or PRs.
- Do not create a PR until B is done.
- GitHub comments carry the Claude Code footer.

## 2. Key technical concepts

**Files and build**
- Rex lab files:
  - src/engine.js: physics, runs in Node and the browser.
  - src/app.html: the page.
  - src/static-data.js: the assumption cards.
  - build-data.py writes src/data.js; build.js writes dist/index.html.
- Build line (CLAUDE.md, updated):
  ```
  python build-data.py && node build.js && node test/calibration.js && node test/presence.js && node test/shots.js && node test/powers.js
  ```
  In this container use `python3`.

**Power keys in ctx and state**
- airAbsorb (0–1, default 1), keepForm, unbreakable, ownRecoil, all on by default.
- Legacy keys groundHolds, gentleHold and coolFlight stay in the engine for the old tests.
- Engine helpers: holdsGround, airShare, dragFactor, gripSafe, ownAnchor.

**Powers-off check**
- test/powers.js part 1: 14,936 cases (test/powers-off-cases.js).
- Fixture test/fixtures/powers-off.json, generated from main's engine: `node test/make-powers-off.js <engine-main.js> src/data.js 'main at 3b2d323'`.
- A copy of main's engine is saved at `scratchpad/engine-main.js`.

**Physics models added in B**
- Snowplow in the ground's frame (fastAir):
  - keep = (gm1+2)/(S(1+xx+gm1+S)), with S = sqrt((1+xx)² + 2·gm1·xx).
  - Eair = E(1−keep); the object sweeps k·x of its own masses.
- handAir: the air his throwing hand drives ahead of it.
- Game of catch past 1% of light speed:
  - fireballAt sweeps air at k times the rate.
  - arriveFast flies the chord between their hands; result 'hits-ground' past sqrt(8Rh).
  - relCatch: a momentum-conserving relativistic catch.
- throwPushJ and easyPush: the thrower's push into the ground.
- toGround {J, T}: a push into the ground turned into a Hann-pulse impulseSource, then ppv, plasterReach and ppvNonlinear.
- limbPulse(body) = 2·0.026·sqrt(0.45H/0.9).

**Page machinery for the two-player tests**
- duoFacts / DUO_PRESET_TEST / DUO_VARIANT {'' , real:{unbreakable:false}, air0:{airAbsorb:0}}.
- Jobs 'least', 'least:real', 'preset:e[:v]'.
- duoNoModel; groundShake / groundShakeChip / groundShakeText (model flag via P.groundOf).

**Review workflow**
- Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/rex-gui-b-review.js.
- Five lenses: brief, air, ground, code, copy. Each has a reviewer, then a verifier.
- Args: {round, prior, decisions}. Concurrency is about 2 on this machine.

## 3. Files and code sections

The branch is `claude/rex-gui-b`. Commits:
- bf7ccc2: page and B features
- 2318d14: round 1 fixes
- 495f6c8: STATUS (latest, pushed)

**src/engine.js** (round 1 changes)

fastAir was rewritten to return:
```
{ k, column, x, gm1, unit, colLen, Eair, Eair0, keep, E: Eair, dHalf, vOut, outweighs: x < 1 }
```

handAir:
```js
function handAir(body, obj, v, gamma) {
  const { style, hands } = throwStyle(obj);
  const d = style === 'whip' ? body.strokes.whip : body.strokes.throw, area = hands * body.palmArea;
  const mAir = K.rho0 * area * d, vv = Math.min(v, K.c);
  return { mAir, area, d, E: isFinite(gamma) ? gamma * mAir * vv * vv : Infinity };
}
```
It is exported as P.handAir. **Round 2 says this needs γ² and a cap.**

throwBlast, relativistic branch:
```
k>=1 → {land:Eobj, path:0}
else hand = handAir(...).E
k===0 → {land:0, path:hand}
else land = Eobj*fa.Eair/fa.Eair0, path = hand
```
- blastFrom gives 'path' when path > land for relativistic throws.

fireballAt:
- `xg = D/unit*k` and `xr = D/sweep*k` when k < 1.
- `Egap = heatAt(xg)`.
- Reports `out.sweepK = sweep/kAir`.
- rBlast uses sweepK.

leg():
- keptFire {kept:true} on fireball returns.
- fast.E is carried.
- arriveFast uses chord geometry (th from atan2, time = chord/v, angleDeg = 0, out.chord). If the chord dips underground, out.hitsGround = {at, path, deepest}.
- After out.recoil:
  - toGroundT = {J: throwPushJ(...), T: max(limbPulse, tPush)}.
  - The hitsGround branch adds E, crater (angleDeg = −th), quake, result 'hits-ground' and miss {..., hits: true}, then returns.
- toGroundC uses k.relativistic ? (k.uAfter > 0 ? 0 : k.pIn) : old.

relCatch(ctxC, obj, v, gammaDeg, w):
- M1 = sqrt(m² + mh² + 2γ·m·mh); E1 = (M1 − m − mh)c².
- held = bolted or FA ≤ R.
- Otherwise Mf from Etot and pIn; uAfter; Ediss; carried = uAfter ≥ 1% c.
- Fields: pIn, Ecatch = E1 + Ediss, sinkRatioRaw.
- catchIt calls it for every v ≥ 1% c. **Round 2: this breaks the powers-off identity and has a round-off problem.**
- catchIt returns Object.assign({...}, ctxC.unbreakable ? {sinkRatioRaw} : {}).

Other engine changes:
- easyPush(ctxT, obj, th, vL) returns {p, armMass, mB}.
- throwPushJ(ctxT, obj, th, vL, full, tab).
- recoilOf refactored to use easyPush.
- stompOnce:
  - realBreaks = crater > 0 || (!soil && hole ≥ 0.01).
  - absorbed = realBreaks ? E : 0.
  - holeDepth = rr.hole when not breaking.
- chargeSpeed calls stomp with stompLaunch: true.
- instantGrowth returns toGround {J: g.m·vSole, T: tau} when unbreakable (and not groundHolds) and dH > 0. It uses Object.assign(extra, {...}).
- shoveOnce: Jfeet = (pB > 0 ? pB + fB.R·t : Fpush·t) − pA, using push.* values. **Round 2 asks for the post-follow-through values instead.**
- armWrestle: toGround J = vToMomentum(v, M).

**src/app.html** (rounds B and 1)
- fastThrowText was rewritten:
  - away(u) gives escape text: galaxy threshold es.galaxyHi; Sun threshold es.sun·(1 + SQRT1_2).
  - handTxt.
  - Main's exact text at share 0 with keepForm off.

- duoFacts:

- Catch chips: carried, kept fireball, hits-ground, sinkRatioRaw "The ground holds".
- Catch items: the aim item is skipped at 100%; the air-wall length is divided by (1 − share).
- Stomp: ownSavedS and the sOwn0 comparison; planet-scale wording when taken; "taken back as growth".

args.prompt:
You are reviewing a change to the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a self-contained HTML page (a claude.ai Artifact) that simulates Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded; read its "Default powers", "Absorption", "Growth details" and "Restraint" canon). The change is on branch claude/rex-gui-b and implements section 5 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("Four new powers, on by default"; read "Rules for every item" and section 5 first; section 6 is a later pull request). In short: four powers on by default replace Comic ground, Gentle hold and Cool flight: Air resistance absorbed (state.airAbsorb 0-1, a slider; engine ctx.airAbsorb, dragFactor = 1 - share on every flight of a thrown or held thing), Things keep their form (ctx.keepForm), Unbreakable footing (ctx.unbreakable: the ground never breaks but its push and shaking stay; engine holdsGround(c)), They take their own recoil (ctx.ownRecoil: recoil goes through the feet into the planet as if bolted). The engine keeps the legacy keys groundHolds/gentleHold/coolFlight unchanged for the old tests. With all four off, every engine result must equal main's (test/powers.js part 1 hashes 15,541 cases against test/fixtures/powers-off.json written from main's engine). New: pushes into the ground (toGround {J, T}) give ground shaking via the stomp's ground-wave model; the two-player tests gain ground shaking in their harm check and the six not-so-heroic presets (duoFacts, DUO_PRESET_TEST, makeDuoPlan jobs and variants); the Throw tab's very fast throws fly a straight line (straightThrow) with a relativistic snowplow (fastAir); the lower-the-slider hint; the break-the-ground preset on real ground.
See the diff: git -C /home/user/rex-strength-lab diff main...claude/rex-gui-b (main's page build: git show main:rex-strength-lab/dist/index.html; main's engine: git show main:rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js). Code: src/engine.js (search holdsGround, airShare, dragFactor, gripSafe, ownAnchor, dragK, toGround, limbPulse, straightThrow, fastAir, handAir, fireballAt, arriveFast, hitsGround, relCatch, throwPushJ, easyPush, catchLeg/leg, tossPartner, throwOnce, jumpOnce, stompOnce, punchOnce, pull, armWrestle, shoveOnce, collide, groundUnderWeight, footprint, RESTRAINT plan/atReal, MOVES, throwBlast), src/app.html (search airAbsorb, keepForm, unbreakable, ownRecoil, renderAirAbsorb, airMeaning, groundShake, duoFacts, makeDuoPlan, resolveDuoEffort, duoEffortBox, duoNoModel, resolveEffort, AIR_PRESETS, stepSide, effortReadout offBy, fastThrowText, bayThrow, bayCatch, legVerdict, catchPartner, wrestleThrow, wrestleShove, bayArm, bayCollide, bayStomp, bayWeight, the state migration near 'The four default powers replaced'), src/static-data.js (assumption cards), research/final-environment.json (sun/galaxy escape facts) and research/reviews/gui-b-escape-facts.json, build-data.py, README.md (Known limits), test/powers.js, test/powers-off-cases.js, test/make-powers-off.js, test/shots.js.
Build: cd /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab && python3 build-data.py && node build.js. Tests: node test/calibration.js (80 s), node test/presence.js (60 s), node test/shots.js (4 min; writes dist/preview.html and shots/), node test/powers.js (3 min; --skip-off skips the 75 s powers-off part; 76 checks). Engine in Node: const P = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js'); data: global.window = {}; require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/data.js'); const D = window.DINO_DATA; bodies: P.makeBody({ build: 'rex', H: 3.048, m: 3007 }); a ctx is { F: kg * P.K.g, mode: 'comic'|'real', body, surface: D.surfaces.find(s => s.id === 'concrete'), anchor: 'friction'|'bolted', airAbsorb, keepForm, unbreakable, ownRecoil, use }. Render pages with Playwright: require('/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright'); chromium.launch({ executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome' }); wrap dist/index.html in '<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"></head><body>' + html + '</body></html>' and load it from a file URL under your scratch folder. Settings persist in localStorage key 'rex-lab-v1' (these reset on every load: effort, absorb, growWhat, stepEffort, duoEffort, oEffortOwn, oSame; pick efforts with the #effort / #duo-effort selects). window.DinoPhys is the engine, window.DINO_DATA the data. Searches finish in the background: wait until no 'working it out' / 'Working out' text remains.
The author's recorded decisions (check whether each is justified by the physics and the code, and stated where the owner will see it; do not report a decision as a defect just because it departs from the brief's letter, unless it is wrong or unjustified):
1. Every new behaviour is gated by its power; with all four off the engine equals main (powers-off fingerprint, 15,541 cases, regenerated from main's engine) and the page's saved-state comparisons run with the powers off. New result fields appear only when a power is on. Consequence (documented in README): with Unbreakable footing and They take their own recoil both off, a throw's or two-player push's own shaking at his feet, a jump's push-off and a pull's rope aren't counted (main didn't count them), so turning them off can lower the shaking shown.
2. 'Break the ground' sets Unbreakable footing aside for that preset only (its search, effort, courtesy ceiling and the tab shown run on real ground). Not for a custom effort past it: all-out is past it, so every all-out result would break the ground, and the ceiling (worked out with the power on) could sit past the break. The two-player 'ground' preset does the same, with its own real-ground ceiling (Collide keeps the hit's push there through collide's toGround option).
3. The arm-wrestling table counts as a held thing (Things keep their form holds it).
4. They take their own recoil covers his throw, punch, stomp (not Collide's stomp-launch), a pull (only the rope's pull back; his legs still need friction), a shove, the thrower in Catch and Wrestle; not arm wrestling, the push match or Collide. A clap has no net recoil. A punch into air leaves the ground no net push: the arm's stop hands it back within the leg pulse.
5. Their own bodies meet real air: at any share above 0% his hand's own air past sound counts (gamma^2 m_air v^2, an upper bound, capped at his push's work), and so does his foot's in a stomp with Unbreakable footing; at 0% main's count is kept (no hand). At 100% the boom stays (his hand).
6. The near-field blast from a throw below 1% of light speed is (1 - share) x what real air takes from the same throw (one more flight at the full drag), so a 50% throw's flight blast is half the 0% one; the game of catch's blast uses the slowed flight's drag times the share (its legs fly once; README says it runs lower, about a third to a half of 0% at 50%).
7. Past 1% of light speed both tabs use a relativistic snowplow in which the object sweeps air at the share of the rate. In the ground's frame the air takes E(1 - keep). Close to light speed a small share of a long column still takes almost all the energy (the All-Star baseball at 50%: over 99.9% of the 0% value); the brief's 'half' holds only for something that sweeps little air (the Great Pyramid straight up just past 1% c: 52%; 84% level).
8. The Throw tab's text at 0% with Things keep their form off is main's; other settings get new texts from the same model.
9. Energy taken back from the air stays with the object; it doesn't feed growth.
10. The ocean figures are the drag the air would have taken along the path actually flown.
11. Not modelled: Everest hitting a bird / the Moon (no thrown-object collisions besides the landing); ice and a steel deck have no ground-wave model (the page says so).
12. 'The Collide charge into an immovable object shakes the ground' is tested with Rex bolted (the page's immovable object), now with Ollie jumping onto him at a 1,000 t dial: Collide's push reaches the ground over at least a limb's contact time, so the default sprint doesn't crack plaster at 5 m. The infinite-mass thought experiment needs no ground; standing Rex hit sideways slides and the plaster preset says it never cracks plaster.
13. Two-player ground shaking only with the powers on; with them off the presets say the shaking isn't modelled; a thrown partner's landing stays a source as before.
14. The lower-the-slider hint shows only on Throw and Catch, only for the air presets, only when the same search at 0% finds an effort (with the hand's air counted, a baseball reaches windows at 100% through his hand; the tests use a car).
15. Old saves pick up all four on, even a saved Comic ground or Gentle hold that was off.
16. CLAUDE.md's build line and CI gained node test/powers.js.
17. Canon question for the owner (also in STATUS Waiting on): with Unbreakable footing on, instant growth can't drive his soles into the ground, so he grows upward from them (as on Comic ground); the ground's push that starts his rise still shakes it.
18. Two-player presets have no least-disruptive floor: there least disruptive is the hardest harmless effort (a ceiling), so a preset is simply the least shared effort that does it.
19. Pre-existing and left as is (powers-off identity): below 100% the game of catch aims a fireball throw with the curvature term of the wrong sign. Page-only corrections that change powers-off text were made where they fixed false statements: shaking 'from the fireball'; 'from him' for a throw that never lands (main said 'from where it lands'); Collide's immovable thought experiment citing a slide; no-ground-wave-model wording on ice; the two-player courtesy ceiling counts broken ground as harm (main called an effort harmless while showing the rock around Rex's bolts cracking, or the ground tearing out around both bolts in the shoving match) and says when a test doesn't judge shaking.
20. A stomp in soil with Unbreakable footing keeps the print the Walk tab allows (sand and gravel: the print where the ground starts to fail; clay: none); deeper sinking and all of the stomp's energy are taken back.
21. Pull shaking is counted only with They take their own recoil and not bolted (a steady load over seconds; it shakes far less than a blow).
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first (see CLAUDE.md). Do NOT edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab and do not commit; work on copies. Write scratch scripts and screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewB3/ (create it; use a subfolder named for your lens). Every finding must be reproduced: give the exact input or place, what the page or code does (quote it, or the script output), what is correct and why (with numbers), and a minimal fix. Report real defects only: wrong physics or formulas, momentum or energy bookkeeping errors, behaviour the brief requires that is missing or wrong, results that changed when the powers are off, wrong or unsupported claims, contradictions between page text and engine numbers, broken layout or controls, accessibility failures, bugs in state handling or background searches, tests that don't test what they say. Skip style preferences.

This is review round 3. Earlier rounds found and fixed the items summarised below; check that each fix holds and look for regressions and anything missed:
Round 1 (52 findings, all confirmed; record research/reviews/gui-b-round1.json) led to these fixes, now at commit 2318d14:

Round 2 is done and pushed. Review round 3 is running now.

**Round 2:** the second review found 49 problems, and a second agent reproduced every one in code. All 49 are fixed. The record is `research/reviews/gui-b-round2.json`. The main fixes:

- **His hand meets real air.** The air his hand pushes ahead of it now counts as a blast whenever it moves faster than sound, not only past 1% of light speed. I corrected the formula and capped it at the energy of his push. A stomp with Unbreakable footing on now counts his foot's air the same way.
- **The fastest catch had a rounding error.** At extreme masses the catch formula rounded its main term to zero, and it ran even with all four powers off. I rewrote it to avoid the rounding and limited it to throws that met no air. With the powers off, all 15,541 engine results match `main` again.
- **A catcher knocked away near light speed.** His own body meets real air, so his flight now counts as a blast, and there is no round trip. A fast throw that hits the ground now shows its crater and quake.
- **Pushes into the ground.**
  - For a throw, the ground now keeps only the object's momentum: the follow-through hands the arm's momentum back.
  - A punch into the air leaves the ground no net push.
  - A Collide hit now reaches the ground through Rex's legs, spread over a footstep's contact time. So the default sprint into a bolted Rex no longer cracks plaster 5 m away.
- **The two-player safe-effort limits now count broken ground.** This changes one thing with all four powers off. `main` called some efforts harmless while its own page showed the rock cracking around Rex's bolts. The page-comparison test now checks those cases at all-out against new reference results recorded from `main`'s page, and checks the corrected limit separately.

All four test suites pass on commit `908af16`.

**Next:** round 3, then fixes if it finds anything. Then I'll open pull request B with the decisions and one canon question for you and the collaborator: should instant growth with Unbreakable footing on grow Rex upward from his soles? Then I'll stop and tell you.

1. Every new behaviour is gated by its power (the hand's and body's own air: by any power); with all four off the engine equals main (powers-off fingerprint, 15,541 cases, regenerated from main's engine) and the page's saved-state comparisons run with the powers off. New result fields appear only when a power is on. The two-player 'ground' preset does the same, with its own real-ground ceiling (Collide keeps the hit's push there through collide's toGround option).
3. The arm-wrestling table counts as a held thing (Things keep their form holds it).
4. They take their own recoil covers his throw, punch, stomp (not Collide's stomp-launch), a pull (only the rope's pull back; his legs still need friction), a shove, the thrower in Catch and Wrestle; not arm wrestling, the push match or Collide. 5. Their own bodies meet real air: with any of their powers on, his hand's own air past sound counts (gamma^2 m_air v^2, an upper bound, capped at his push's work), his foot's in a stomp with Unbreakable footing, and his body's in a supersonic jump; with all four off main's count is kept (the 0% read-out says so). At 100% the boom stays (his hand).
6. The Throw tab's blast near him is (1 - share) x what real air takes from the same throw (one more flight at the full drag; all of its energy if real air never brings it down, an upper bound; past 1% of light speed all of its energy, main's count), one rule on both sides of 1% c, so 50% gives half the 0% blast. The game of catch counts what the air takes from the slowed flight between them (all of that flight is near them).
7. Past 1% of light speed the text reports the air's whole-path take from a relativistic snowplow sweeping air at the share of the rate (in the ground's frame E(1 - keep); close to light speed nearly all of it at any share below 100%), while the blast near him follows decision 6 (so the brief's 'half at 50%' holds for the blast). The game of catch's fireballs use the same snowplow.
8. The Throw tab's text at 0% with Things keep their form off is main's; other settings get new texts from the same model.
9. Energy taken back from the air stays with the object; it doesn't feed growth.
10. The ocean figures are the drag the air would have taken along the path actually flown.
11. Not modelled: Everest hitting a bird / the Moon (no thrown-object collisions besides the landing); ice and a steel deck have no ground-wave model (the page says so).
12. 'The Collide charge into an immovable object shakes the ground' is tested with Rex bolted (the page's immovable object), now with Ollie jumping onto him at a 1,000 t dial: Collide's push reaches the ground over at least a limb's contact time, so the default sprint doesn't crack plaster at 5 m. The infinite-mass thought experiment needs no ground; standing Rex hit sideways slides and the plaster preset says it never cracks plaster.
13. Two-player ground shaking only with the powers on; with them off the presets say the shaking isn't modelled; a thrown partner's landing stays a source as before.
14. The lower-the-slider hint shows only on Throw and Catch, only for the air presets, only when the same search at 0% finds an effort (with the hand's air counted, a baseball reaches windows at 100% through his hand; the tests use a car).
15. Old saves pick up all four on, even a saved Comic ground or Gentle hold that was off.
16. CLAUDE.md's build line and CI gained node test/powers.js.
17. Canon question for the owner (also in STATUS Waiting on): with Unbreakable footing on, instant growth can't drive his soles into the ground, so he grows upward from them (as on Comic ground); the ground's push that starts his rise still shakes it.
18. Two-player presets have no least-disruptive floor: there least disruptive is the hardest harmless effort (a ceiling), so a preset is simply the least shared effort that does it.
19. Pre-existing and left as is (powers-off identity): below 100% the game of catch aims a fireball throw with the curvature term of the wrong sign. Page-only corrections that change powers-off text were made where they fixed false statements: shaking 'from the fireball'; 'from him' for a throw that never lands (main said 'from where it lands'); Collide's immovable thought experiment citing a slide; no-ground-wave-model wording on ice; the two-player courtesy ceiling counts broken ground as harm (main called an effort harmless while showing the rock around Rex's bolts cracking, or the ground tearing out around both bolts in the shoving match) and says when a test doesn't judge shaking.
20. A stomp in soil with Unbreakable footing keeps the print the Walk tab allows (sand and gravel: the print where the ground starts to fail; clay: none); deeper sinking and all of its energy are taken back.
21. Pull shaking is counted only with They take their own recoil (bolted too: the rope's pull goes through his bolts); with the power off main's count (none).
22. Canon's weak-ground exception: where the ground couldn't bear a push, it takes only what it can (its bearing beyond his weight over the pulse; for a throw or a catch its share of the downward push) and their power supplies the rest, which goes to the endless ocean ('supplied'). The stomp keeps real ground's pulse (its foot momentum is stopped by the ground either way).
23. A quick arm-wrestling pin (its swing shorter than a limb's contact time) leaves the ground no net push, like a punch; a slower pin keeps the slam's blow. A stomp's shaking counts only the foot's blow (an upper bound: the pull through his standing foot partly cancels it), stated on the page.
24. The two-player courtesy ceiling counts a supersonic arm pin with a power on (with them off the table breaks first, as on main).

The change is on branch claude/rex-gui-b and implements section 5 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("Four new powers, on by default"; read "Rules for every item" and section 5 first; section 6 is a later pull request). In short: four powers on by default replace Comic ground, Gentle hold and Cool flight: Air resistance absorbed (state.airAbsorb 0-1, a slider; engine ctx.airAbsorb, dragFactor = 1 - share on every flight of a thrown or held thing), Things keep their form (ctx.keepForm), Unbreakable footing (ctx.unbreakable: the ground never breaks but its push and shaking stay; engine holdsGround(c)), They take their own recoil (ctx.ownRecoil: recoil goes through the feet into the planet as if bolted). See the diff: git -C /home/user/rex-strength-lab diff main...claude/rex-gui-b (main's page build: git show main:rex-strength-lab/dist/index.html; main's engine: git show main:rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js). Code: src/engine.js (search holdsGround, airShare, dragFactor, gripSafe, ownAnchor, dragK, toGround, limbPulse, straightThrow, fastAir, handAir, fireballAt, arriveFast, hitsGround, relCatch, throwPushJ, easyPush, catchLeg/leg, tossPartner, throwOnce, jumpOnce, stompOnce, punchOnce, pull, armWrestle, shoveOnce, collide, groundUnderWeight, footprint, RESTRAINT plan/atReal, MOVES, throwBlast), src/app.html (search airAbsorb, keepForm, unbreakable, ownRecoil, renderAirAbsorb, airMeaning, groundShake, duoFacts, makeDuoPlan, resolveDuoEffort, duoEffortBox, duoNoModel, resolveEffort, AIR_PRESETS, stepSide, effortReadout offBy, fastThrowText, bayThrow, bayCatch, legVerdict, catchPartner, wrestleThrow, wrestleShove, bayArm, bayCollide, bayStomp, bayWeight, the state migration near 'The four default powers replaced'), src/static-data.js (assumption cards), research/final-environment.json (sun/galaxy escape facts) and research/reviews/gui-b-escape-facts.json, build-data.py, README.md (Known limits), test/powers.js, test/powers-off-cases.js, test/make-powers-off.js, test/shots.js.
Build: cd /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab && python3 build-data.py && node build.js. Tests: node test/calibration.js (80 s), node test/presence.js (60 s), node test/shots.js (4 min; writes dist/preview.html and shots/), node test/powers.js (3 min; --skip-off skips the 75 s powers-off part; 86 checks). Engine in Node: const P = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js'); data: global.window = {}; require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/data.js'); const D = window.DINO_DATA; bodies: P.makeBody({ build: 'rex', H: 3.048, m: 3007 }); a ctx is { F: kg * P.K.g, mode: 'comic'|'real', body, surface: D.surfaces.find(s => s.id === 'concrete'), anchor: 'friction'|'bolted', airAbsorb, keepForm, unbreakable, ownRecoil, use }. Render pages with Playwright: require('/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright'); chromium.launch({ executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome' }); wrap dist/index.html in '<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"></head><body>' + html + '</body></html>' and load it from a file URL under your scratch folder. Settings persist in localStorage key 'rex-lab-v1' (these reset on every load: effort, absorb, growWhat, stepEffort, duoEffort, oEffortOwn, oSame; pick efforts with the #effort / #duo-effort selects). window.DinoPhys is the engine, window.DINO_DATA the data. Searches finish in the background: wait until no 'working it out' / 'Working out' text remains.
The author's recorded decisions (check whether each is justified by the physics and the code, and stated where the owner will see it; do not report a decision as a defect just because it departs from the brief's letter, unless it is wrong or unjustified):
1. Every new behaviour is gated by its power (the hand's and body's own air: by any power); with all four off the engine equals main (powers-off fingerprint, 15,541 cases, regenerated from main's engine) and the page's saved-state comparisons run with the powers off. New result fields appear only when a power is on. Consequence (documented in README): with Unbreakable footing and They take their own recoil both off, a throw's or two-player push's own shaking at his feet, a jump's push-off and a pull's rope aren't counted (main didn't count them), so turning them off can lower the shaking shown.
2. 'Break the ground' sets Unbreakable footing aside for that preset only (its search, effort, courtesy ceiling and the tab shown run on real ground). Not for a custom effort past it: all-out is past it, so every all-out result would break the ground, and the ceiling (worked out with the power on) could sit past the break. The two-player 'ground' preset does the same, with its own real-ground ceiling (Collide keeps the hit's push there through collide's toGround option).
3. The arm-wrestling table counts as a held thing (Things keep their form holds it).
4. They take their own recoil covers his throw, punch, stomp (not Collide's stomp-launch), a pull (only the rope's pull back; his legs still need friction), a shove, the thrower in Catch and Wrestle; not arm wrestling, the push match or Collide. A clap has no net recoil. A punch into air leaves the ground no net push: the arm's stop hands it back within the leg pulse.
5. Their own bodies meet real air: with any of their powers on, his hand's own air past sound counts (gamma^2 m_air v^2, an upper bound, capped at his push's work), his foot's in a stomp with Unbreakable footing, and his body's in a supersonic jump; with all four off main's count is kept (the 0% read-out says so). At 100% the boom stays (his hand).
6. The Throw tab's blast near him is (1 - share) x what real air takes from the same throw (one more flight at the full drag; all of its energy if real air never brings it down, an upper bound; past 1% of light speed all of its energy, main's count), one rule on both sides of 1% c, so 50% gives half the 0% blast. The game of catch counts what the air takes from the slowed flight between them (all of that flight is near them).
7. Past 1% of light speed the text reports the air's whole-path take from a relativistic snowplow sweeping air at the share of the rate (in the ground's frame E(1 - keep); close to light speed nearly all of it at any share below 100%), while the blast near him follows decision 6 (so the brief's 'half at 50%' holds for the blast). The game of catch's fireballs use the same snowplow.
8. The Throw tab's text at 0% with Things keep their form off is main's; other settings get new texts from the same model.
9. Energy taken back from the air stays with the object; it doesn't feed growth.
10. The ocean figures are the drag the air would have taken along the path actually flown.
11. Not modelled: Everest hitting a bird / the Moon (no thrown-object collisions besides the landing); ice and a steel deck have no ground-wave model (the page says so).
12. 'The Collide charge into an immovable object shakes the ground' is tested with Rex bolted (the page's immovable object), now with Ollie jumping onto him at a 1,000 t dial: Collide's push reaches the ground over at least a limb's contact time, so the default sprint doesn't crack plaster at 5 m. The infinite-mass thought experiment needs no ground; standing Rex hit sideways slides and the plaster preset says it never cracks plaster.
13. Two-player ground shaking only with the powers on; with them off the presets say the shaking isn't modelled; a thrown partner's landing stays a source as before.
14. The lower-the-slider hint shows only on Throw and Catch, only for the air presets, only when the same search at 0% finds an effort (with the hand's air counted, a baseball reaches windows at 100% through his hand; the tests use a car).
15. Old saves pick up all four on, even a saved Comic ground or Gentle hold that was off.
16. CLAUDE.md's build line and CI gained node test/powers.js.
17. Canon question for the owner (also in STATUS Waiting on): with Unbreakable footing on, instant growth can't drive his soles into the ground, so he grows upward from them (as on Comic ground); the ground's push that starts his rise still shakes it.
18. Two-player presets have no least-disruptive floor: there least disruptive is the hardest harmless effort (a ceiling), so a preset is simply the least shared effort that does it.
19. Pre-existing and left as is (powers-off identity): below 100% the game of catch aims a fireball throw with the curvature term of the wrong sign. Page-only corrections that change powers-off text were made where they fixed false statements: shaking 'from the fireball'; 'from him' for a throw that never lands (main said 'from where it lands'); Collide's immovable thought experiment citing a slide; no-ground-wave-model wording on ice; the two-player courtesy ceiling counts broken ground as harm (main called an effort harmless while showing the rock around Rex's bolts cracking, or the ground tearing out around both bolts in the shoving match) and says when a test doesn't judge shaking.
20. A stomp in soil with Unbreakable footing keeps the print the Walk tab allows (sand and gravel: the print where the ground starts to fail; clay: none); deeper sinking and all of its energy are taken back.
21. Pull shaking is counted only with They take their own recoil (bolted too: the rope's pull goes through his bolts); with the power off main's count (none).
22. Canon's weak-ground exception: where the ground couldn't bear a push, it takes only what it can (its bearing beyond his weight over the pulse; for a throw or a catch its share of the downward push) and their power supplies the rest, which goes to the endless ocean ('supplied'). The stomp keeps real ground's pulse (its foot momentum is stopped by the ground either way).
23. A quick arm-wrestling pin (its swing shorter than a limb's contact time) leaves the ground no net push, like a punch; a slower pin keeps the slam's blow. A stomp's shaking counts only the foot's blow (an upper bound: the pull through his standing foot partly cancels it), stated on the page.
24. The two-player courtesy ceiling counts a supersonic arm pin with a power on (with them off the table breaks first, as on main).
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first (see CLAUDE.md). Do NOT edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab and do not commit; work on copies. Write scratch scripts and screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewB4/ (create it; use a subfolder named for your lens). Every finding must be reproduced: give the exact input or place, what the page or code does (quote it, or the script output), what is correct and why (with numbers), and a minimal fix. Report real defects only: wrong physics or formulas, momentum or energy bookkeeping errors, behaviour the brief requires that is missing or wrong, results that changed when the powers are off, wrong or unsupported claims, contradictions between page text and engine numbers, broken layout or controls, accessibility failures, bugs in state handling or background searches, tests that don't test what they say. Skip style preferences.

This is review round 4. Earlier rounds found and fixed the items summarised below; check that each fix holds and look for regressions and anything missed:
Rounds 1-3 (52, 49 and 45 findings; records research/reviews/gui-b-round1.json to gui-b-round3.json, each finding with its outcome) are summarised in those files. Focus on round 3's fixes (now at commit 43d7465; git -C /home/user/rex-strength-lab diff 908af16 43d7465 shows them; the full change is main...claude/rex-gui-b), check that each holds, and look for regressions they caused and anything still missed.

Round 3's fixes:
- relCatch takes the arriving momentum and rest mass (catchIt/relCatch 'fin': the fireball's conserved p and the lump's rest mass mLump for the near-100% sheath; p from the throw's energy at 100%, since near c the speed rounds; an unbounded branch for infinite strength). fireballAt reports mLump only when Things keep their form applies (powers-off identity).
- Canon's weak-ground exception: where the ground couldn't bear a push it takes only what it can and their power supplies the rest ('supplied', to the endless ocean): jump push-off (min(p, (bearing - weight) x T)) and landing pulses (MOVES.jump.shake, landBear), throw toGround (its downward part / sinkRatioRaw), catch toGroundC (likewise), Collide held from above by Unbreakable footing (min(J, real bearing x T)), instant growth (min(m vSole, (soles x q - weight) x tau)). Page: suppliedText on those items; the Jump and Throw texts.
- One near-field blast rule on both sides of 1% c (throwBlast): past 1% c the blast is (1 - share) x its energy; the snowplow's whole-path take only in the text. His hand's air counts whenever any power is on (anyPower) on Throw, Catch legs, the partner toss and Wrestle; with all four off it is main's count (the 0% read-out says so with all powers off). The game of catch's blast counts the slowed flight's own take (L.drag.E), no second factor of the share.
- Pull: shaking with They take their own recoil whether or not bolted; ropeT whenever the power is on. Partner toss (tossPartner): toGroundT, toGroundC (capped), hand air; duoFacts judges it. Arm pin: no net push when the swing is shorter than a limb's contact time; the two-player arm check counts a supersonic pin or drag (with a power on). Jump: with any power on, airLoss (what the air takes from his flight) counts as blast past sound. Catch shock pressure gamma^2 rho v^2 on a relativistic arrival (gated on the fast path).
- Page: the All-Star verdict ('no fireball around it' + the hand's), keep-form exits between 1 km/s and escape, the ocean text (can exceed its energy; keeps its speed), the escaping-throw blast label, galaxy thresholds measured from Earth, dHalf wording, the duplicate chip, the Throw math line, the sheath texts at any share, items up to 10 on Throw/Jump/Stomp/Catch/Wrestle throw, own-recoil credits only where he would be shoved back without it, the effort box credits a power only where the hazard happens with it off (offHappens, all-out), calibration check with the powers off, reasons for Sprint/Clap/Pull/Punch shaking, the standing push match's ground reason, the stomp's upper-bound caveat, 'On real ground, the concrete slab...'.
- Tests: powers.js 86 checks (sheath and gamma 1e25-1e30 and infinite catches, carried energy, weak ground on jump/Collide/growth, no blast step at 1% c, All-Star blast half at 50%, arm pins quick/slow, bolted pull, shove with own recoil only, partner toss, supersonic jump air); shots: Unbreakable footing not left off after the two-player break-the-ground preset, the All-Star regex.

Do not re-report anything a round 1-3 record already lists as fixed unless the fix does not hold (say how), or anything the recorded decisions below cover unless the decision itself is wrong.

LENS: CODE, STATE AND TESTS. (1) The powers-off equivalence: is test/fixtures/powers-off.json really from main's engine (regenerate it from git show main:rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js with test/make-powers-off.js into your scratch folder and compare)? Does test/powers-off-cases.js cover every exported engine function and the code paths the change touched (relativistic throws, catch legs at every result, collide modes, growth, walk, weight, RESTRAINT plans and presets)? Try mutations in a scratch copy of the engine that change a powers-off result in a touched path and see whether part 1 catches them. Does the page's powers-off comparison (shots.js s1/s3/s4 with POWERS_OFF) still compare everything it did before? (2) The page: duoFacts must keep the old duoHarm harm order and fingerprint exactly with the powers off; makeDuoPlan's job/variant searches, stepDuoPlan/duoReady background stepping and cancellation (switching presets mid-search, closing the element, settings changes), the side search for the lower-the-slider hint (stepSide/stopSide), the break-the-ground preset's real flag and the temporary state.unbreakable override during the two-player render (can it leak if a render throws? can save() run while it is overridden?), the migration of old saves (groundHolds/gentleHold/coolFlight dropped, new defaults on, validators), planFor/duoKey/thKey keys include every power. (3) Tests: do test/powers.js and the new shots.js checks really test what they say? Break the page or engine in a scratch copy (e.g. make a preset move the slider, drop the hint, ignore airAbsorb in fly, let ownRecoil slide him, give toGround the wrong sign, remove the real-ground run) and see whether a test fails. Flakiness (fixed waits). CI (.github/workflows/test.yml) runs powers.js; will the 20-minute job timeout hold?

Under verified_ok, list what you checked and found correct. Prefix finding ids with "code-".

Round 3 is fixed and pushed (`43d7465`), and review round 4 is now running in the background.

**Round 3** found 45 problems. A second agent reproduced 43 in code; the other 2 didn't hold up. All 43 are fixed. The record is `research/reviews/gui-b-round3.json`. The main fixes:

- **Very fast catches lost most of the throw's momentum.** This was the one critical finding.
  - Near 100% air resistance absorbed, a catch was freed less than 1% of the throw's energy.
  - Past about γ 10⁷, the catch worked from a speed that rounds to light speed, so it was wrong too.
  - The catch now uses the momentum and mass that actually arrive. Tests check 50%, 99% and 100%, and dials up to infinite strength.
- **Weak ground now follows canon.** CLAUDE.md says that where the ground can't bear a push, "their power supplies it". The engine had been putting the whole push into the ground anyway, so the shaking on sand was overstated about 15–60 times. Now the ground takes only what it can bear, and the rest goes to the endless ocean. This applies to the jump, the throw, the catch, a Collide hit from above, and instant growth.
- **The blast now uses one rule below and above 1% of light speed.** Before, a throw's blast jumped 2–10× when its speed crossed that line. With one rule, 50% air resistance absorbed now gives half the 0% blast, as your brief's test expects. The page text still reports the air's take over the whole path separately.
- **Smaller physics fixes:**
  - His hand's own air now counts whenever any power is on, not only above 0% on the slider.
  - A bolted pull now shakes the ground.
  - Tossing Ollie up and catching him is now judged for harm.
  - A quick arm-wrestling pin leaves the ground no net push, like a punch.
  - A supersonic jump's own air now counts as a blast.
- **The effort box now credits a power only where it changed the result.** Before, the opening view credited Unbreakable footing and They take their own recoil even though they changed nothing there.

All four test suites pass:

- calibration: all checks pass
- presence: 383 checks
- `powers.js`: 88 checks, including all 15,541 powers-off comparisons with `main`
- shots: all checks pass

**Why a round 4:** each round has found a little less (52, 49, 43), but round 3 still turned up a critical bug. So round 4 checks round 3's fixes before I open pull request B. After it, I'll fix what it finds, open the pull request with the decisions and the canon question about growth with Unbreakable footing on, and then stop and tell you.

   **src/engine.js — round 4 changes (uncommitted)**

   `weakGround` (after `limbPulse`):
   ```js
   function weakGround(ctx, body, J, th, T, weight) {
     if (!ctx.unbreakable || !isFinite(J) || !(J > 0) || !(T > 0)) return { J };
     const bear = Math.max(0, qultFor(ctx.surface, body.footB) * 2 * body.footArea - weight), cap = bear * T;
     const Jd = J * Math.max(0, Math.sin(th)), Jh = J * Math.cos(th);
     if (!(Jd > cap)) return { J };
     return { J: Math.hypot(Jh, cap), whole: J, supplied: Jd - cap };
   }
   ```

text:
Round 4 is done: 31 confirmed findings are fixed and pushed to `claude/rex-gui-b` as `e692a27`. Round 5 of the adversarial review is now running. It checks that round 4's fixes hold and looks for anything they broke. Pull request B isn't open yet.

The full Rex lab test line passes on `e692a27`:
- calibration: all checks pass.
- presence: 383 checks pass.
- shots: no overflow, errors or broken text at 390 px and 1280 px, light and dark.
- `test/powers.js`: 96 of 96 pass. That includes the check that with all four powers off, all 15,541 engine results still match `main` exactly.

What changed in round 4:
- **One rule for weak ground under every push.** The ground now takes only what it can bear beyond the weight already on it, and their power supplies the rest. Before, the rule for throws was inconsistent: harder throws shook the ground less, and gentle throws skipped the limit entirely. It now covers gentle throws, tossing Ollie, the stomp and a jump at unlimited strength too.
- **Tossing Ollie** (the Catch tab with Ollie as the ball) now shows what its effort setting is judged on: the push into the ground, how far it shakes, the part their power supplies, and the air his hands hit. Very fast tosses get the same text as the Throw tab.
- **Very fast throws** on the Throw tab, the Wrestle throw and the toss all state now how much Earth's gravity bends the path and where the thrown thing ends up. That fixed a false line: between 11.2 and 16.7 km/s the page said leaving the solar system "depends on the way it goes", when no direction allows it.
- **Physics fixes:**
  - A drag-free level throw at orbital speed is now reported as an orbit. Before, it ran millions of steps and said "still in flight".
  - A very fast catch no longer flips between "caught" and "no hands can catch that" at an arbitrary 1% cut-off.
  - Throws straight up are compared by height, not by a range that was only rounding error.
- **Wording fixes** across several tabs. The worst was the shock pressure, which was labelled ρv² while showing half of it.
- **New checks:** eight in `test/powers.js` and one page check for Collide. Two bugs the reviewers deliberately planted, which the old checks missed, now fail.

One round 4 finding got no verdict because its checker failed. Two confirmed findings covered the same issue, and that fix is in.

The record is `rex-strength-lab/research/reviews/gui-b-round4.json`. The README's Known limits and review history are updated, and so is STATUS.md.

**Decision:** I'm running round 5 before opening the pull request. Earlier rounds kept finding that the previous round's fixes only partly held, and the house pattern calls for re-checking fixes. Each round has taken about two hours. After it, I'll fix what it confirms, open pull request B and stop.

The decisions list for the pull request is drafted (26 items). The canon question about growth with Unbreakable footing on is still open in STATUS.md under Waiting on.

Round 5 is done: all 35 findings were confirmed and fixed, and pushed to `claude/rex-gui-b` as `616ced0`. Pull request B isn't open yet. A short check of those fixes is running first.

The full Rex lab test line passes on `616ced0`:
- calibration and presence (383 checks) pass.
- shots: no overflow, errors or broken text in any of the four views.
- `test/powers.js`: 113 of 113, including the check that all 15,541 engine results match `main` with the four powers off.

Main fixes in round 5:
- **Ground caps never reduce shaking.** Round 4's stomp fix had made a harder stomp on sand shake the ground five times less, just past the footprint. The stomp's and the landing's caps now start at what real ground took at that point.
- **Pushes that slipped the cap.** Unlimited-strength pushes now get the weak-ground cap like any other push. When they stand without their recoil taken, the ground's sideways grip is now limited to what its friction can give.
- **Game of catch.** With any power on, a very fast throw below 100% could "reach" Ollie through the planet; past about 12 km it now hits the ground near the thrower. The sheath catch no longer flips to "a blast hits him" at the half-energy point. A missed fast throw no longer "lands at 0 m/s".
- **Far blast reach.** Past 1% of light speed the far reach now counts the energy the air takes within that reach. A car thrown at 90% now reaches as far as at 0%. This means the brief's "50% gives half" test holds near him but not for the far reach; the README and the decisions list say so.
- **Two-player pushes now counted.** Collide includes the charger's weight and his take-off. A shove includes a bolted partner's bolts. The Wrestle throw caps Ollie's landing. The Collide tab drawn for the "break the ground" preset now shows the shaking its effort setting is judged on.
- **Wording.** The worst cases: "the ground can bear it" beside an unbounded push, and "no sinking" on sand where the Stomp tab shows a 9 cm footprint.

The review rounds are not converging: 52, 49, 45, 32, then 35 findings. Each round's fixes add text and rules the next round can check.
