args.prompt:
Project: the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a one-page physics simulator for Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). Read section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)") before anything else: it is the task. Today the page compares every energy to a ladder of eleven references (build-data.py, the 'energy' list; app.html compareEnergy): the fastest pitch (162 J), a Corolla at 100 km/h (0.52 MJ), an M67 hand grenade (1.0 MJ), the MOAB (4.6e10 J), Hiroshima (6.3e13 J), Castle Bravo (6.3e16 J), the Tsar Bomba (2.1e17 J), Krakatoa 1883 (8.4e17 J), the Chicxulub impact (4.2e23 J), the Sun's output for a second (3.8e26 J) and Earth's gravitational binding energy (2.49e32 J). The page names the nearest rung below and a multiple, so it says things like "300 hand grenades". The new rule: a comparison never shows a multiple above about 10x or a share below about 10%, so the ladder needs a rung at least every factor of about 10 (100x at the very most), from about 1 J (the gentlest efforts on the page) to beyond a supernova (the page's energies reach above 1e40 J at the top of its strength dial). One shared ladder, a mix of kinds of event. Existing facts for the current rungs are in /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/research/final-environment.json (keys energy_*), final-humans.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass) and final-objects.json (toyota_corolla_curb_mass): read them so you don't duplicate keys, and reuse their values where they are right.
What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. Give each one a short page phrase that fits "about 3x ___" and "40% of ___" (for example "a lightning bolt", "the Beirut port explosion of 2020"). Kinetic energies computed from a mass and speed are fine (status derived) if the mass and speed are sourced. Avoid jargon; avoid anything grisly or that a general reader would find tasteless as a yardstick beyond the bombs and disasters the page already uses.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first. A number is "verified" only if you fetched the page or PDF yourself and saw the number there; give the exact URL you fetched. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Where the literature gives a range, record low_si and high_si and the value used, and say why that value (the asteroid's existing fact is the model). Note how uncertain each value is: the page gives only a rough multiple ("roughly 3x") for a reference uncertain by more than about 2x either way.
Load web tools with ToolSearch query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch". For PDFs, curl them into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ and extract text with python (pip install --user pypdf if needed) or pdftotext. Keep raw downloads and scripts under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ (create it). Do not edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab.
Fact fields (the lab's research format): key (snake_case, prefix energy_, e.g. energy_lightning_bolt), category ("energy_reference"), label, status (verified = number seen in a fetched primary or authoritative source | derived = computed by you from verified inputs, formula and inputs in notes | estimate = a reasoned assumption | reported = secondary or weak source only | disputed = sources disagree materially), value_si (J, a number), unit_si ("J"), low_si and high_si when there is a range, display (short human text with the original units, e.g. "about 1 GJ per flash (NOAA: typical 1-10 GJ)"), sources (title + exact URL fetched), notes (exact quote or table cell, conditions, caveats; under about 900 characters), who_when, and page_short (the short phrase for the page). For a derived kinetic energy, also give the input facts (mass, speed) as their own facts.

TOPIC "audit": the existing rungs, against the same standard ("Also check, while researching: the existing rungs' values and sources"). For each current rung, re-fetch its sources and try hard to find a better one (primary or authoritative), then give the corrected fact (same key) with an honest status. In particular: the fastest pitch on record (Aroldis Chapman, 105.8 mph, 2010: MLB Statcast or MLB.com; baseball mass from the MLB Official Baseball Rules 3.01: 5 to 5.25 oz); the Corolla's curb mass (Toyota's own spec sheet); the M67 grenade (US Army TC 3-23.30 for the 6.5 oz Composition B fill; a better source than Wikipedia for Comp B's energy, e.g. a detonation-energy or heat-of-detonation figure from a US Army or DoD handbook, LLNL Explosives Handbook, or a journal; the brief allows a range); the MOAB (US Air Force or DoD statements, GlobalSecurity, AFRL; 11 t TNT); Hiroshima (LANL LA-8819, Malik 1985; DOE/OSTI; the Radiation Effects Research Foundation DS02 report gives 16 kt); Castle Bravo (DOE/NV-209 United States Nuclear Tests, on osti.gov or nnss.gov; 15 Mt); the Tsar Bomba (Rosatom, Russian sources, Sublette's archive; 50 Mt); Krakatoa 1883 (a volcanology paper or the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Self & Rampino 1981, Simkin & Fiske 1983; the energy figure is soft); Chicxulub (journal papers; keep a range); the Sun's luminosity (IAU 2015 B3, verified); Earth's binding energy (a textbook or paper, or our PREM integral fact energy_earth_binding_prem_computed in final-density.json). Propose replacements where a rung is too weak or obscure, and keep each fact's key.

Project: the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a one-page physics simulator for Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). Read section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)") before anything else: it is the task. Today the page compares every energy to a ladder of eleven references (build-data.py, the 'energy' list; app.html compareEnergy): the fastest pitch (162 J), a Corolla at 100 km/h (0.52 MJ), an M67 hand grenade (1.0 MJ), the MOAB (4.6e10 J), Hiroshima (6.3e13 J), Castle Bravo (6.3e16 J), the Tsar Bomba (2.1e17 J), Krakatoa 1883 (8.4e17 J), the Chicxulub impact (4.2e23 J), the Sun's output for a second (3.8e26 J) and Earth's gravitational binding energy (2.49e32 J). The page names the nearest rung below and a multiple, so it says things like "300 hand grenades". The new rule: a comparison never shows a multiple above about 10x or a share below about 10%, so the ladder needs a rung at least every factor of about 10 (100x at the very most), from about 1 J (the gentlest efforts on the page) to beyond a supernova (the page's energies reach above 1e40 J at the top of its strength dial). One shared ladder, a mix of kinds of event. Existing facts for the current rungs are in /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/research/final-environment.json (keys energy_*), final-humans.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass) and final-objects.json (toyota_corolla_curb_mass): read them so you don't duplicate keys, and reuse their values where they are right.
What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. Give each one a short page phrase that fits "about 3x ___" and "40% of ___" (for example "a lightning bolt", "the Beirut port explosion of 2020"). Kinetic energies computed from a mass and speed are fine (status derived) if the mass and speed are sourced. Avoid jargon; avoid anything grisly or that a general reader would find tasteless as a yardstick beyond the bombs and disasters the page already uses.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first. A number is "verified" only if you fetched the page or PDF yourself and saw the number there; give the exact URL you fetched. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Where the literature gives a range, record low_si and high_si and the value used, and say why that value (the asteroid's existing fact is the model). Note how uncertain each value is: the page gives only a rough multiple ("roughly 3x") for a reference uncertain by more than about 2x either way.
Load web tools with ToolSearch query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch". For PDFs, curl them into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ and extract text with python (pip install --user pypdf if needed) or pdftotext. Keep raw downloads and scripts under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ (create it). Do not edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab.
Fact fields (the lab's research format): key (snake_case, prefix energy_, e.g. energy_lightning_bolt), category ("energy_reference"), label, status (verified = number seen in a fetched primary or authoritative source | derived = computed by you from verified inputs, formula and inputs in notes | estimate = a reasoned assumption | reported = secondary or weak source only | disputed = sources disagree materially), value_si (J, a number), unit_si ("J"), low_si and high_si when there is a range, display (short human text with the original units, e.g. "about 1 GJ per flash (NOAA: typical 1-10 GJ)"), sources (title + exact URL fetched), notes (exact quote or table cell, conditions, caveats; under about 900 characters), who_when, and page_short (the short phrase for the page). For a derived kinetic energy, also give the input facts (mass, speed) as their own facts.

You are the skeptical fact-checker for topic "small". Below are the researcher's facts and proposed rungs. Fetch EVERY cited source for EVERY fact yourself (list the URLs you fetched in each check), and check each value, unit conversion, range, quotation, date and status against what the source actually says; recompute every derived number with your own script. Mark ok=false with a correction for anything wrong or mislabelled: a number not on the cited page, a secondary summary presented as the primary source, a weak source marked verified, a range collapsed to a point, a wrong unit or TNT conversion (1 t TNT = 4.184e9 J exactly), an uncertainty understated. If a source can't be fetched, say so and downgrade the status unless another fetched source confirms the number. Also judge the proposed rungs as page yardsticks (plain, picturable, not misleading) and list decades in the band still without a rung within 10x. Do not edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab.

1. Primary Request and Intent:

   The user (the owner, in Claude Code cloud sessions) asked for `rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md` to be built as three pull requests, one at a time:
   - **A.** Page organisation (sections 1–4). Merged as #20 and live as version 11.

   - **C.** Energy comparisons (section 6). Research first: a researcher, then a skeptic who fetches every source. In progress now.

   - "Claim rex-strength-lab/ in STATUS.md (and any other files you'll touch), on your own claude/... branch. Release the claim when you finish."
   - Follow the house pattern:
     - every number sourced or labelled an estimate;
     - tests for each change;
     - the full Rex lab build line passes;
     - README and Known limits updated;
     - adversarial review rounds with every finding reproduced in code, and records in `rex-strength-lab/research/reviews/`.
   - "Saved pages still load, with retired settings migrated as each section says."

   ```js
   function compareEnergy(J) {
     if (!isFinite(J)) return 'more than any finite amount';
     const refs = D.energyRefs.slice().sort((a, b) => a.J - b.J);
     let best = null;
     for (const r of refs) if (r.J <= J) best = r;
     if (!best) { const r = refs[0]; return sig(J / r.J * 100, 2) + '% of ' + r.short; }
     const ratio = J / best.J;
     if (ratio < 1.15) return '≈ ' + best.short;
     if (best.id === 'chicxulub') return 'roughly ' + sig(ratio, 1) + '× ' + best.short;
     return big(ratio, 2) + '× ' + best.short;
   }
   ```

   ```js
   function weakGround(ctx, body, J, th, T, weight, bolted) {
     if (!ctx.unbreakable || !(J > 0) || !(T > 0)) return { J };
     const Nmax = qultFor(ctx.surface, body.footB) * 2 * body.footArea, cap = Math.max(0, Nmax - weight) * T;
     const capH = (bolted != null ? bolted : ownAnchor(ctx) === 'bolted') ? Infinity : (ctx.surface.mu || 0) * Nmax * T;
     const sn = Math.sin(th), cs = Math.abs(Math.cos(th));
     const Jd = sn > 1e-12 ? J * sn : 0, Jh = cs < 1e-9 ? 0 : J * cs;
     if (!(Jd > cap) && !(Jh > capH)) return { J };
     const Jdg = Math.min(Jd, cap), Jhg = Math.min(Jh, capH), sD = Jd > Jdg ? Jd - Jdg : 0, sH = Jh > Jhg ? Jh - Jhg : 0;
   ```

Project: the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a one-page physics simulator for Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). Read section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)") before anything else: it is the task. Today the page compares every energy to a ladder of eleven references (build-data.py, the 'energy' list; app.html compareEnergy): the fastest pitch (162 J), a Corolla at 100 km/h (0.52 MJ), an M67 hand grenade (1.0 MJ), the MOAB (4.6e10 J), Hiroshima (6.3e13 J), Castle Bravo (6.3e16 J), the Tsar Bomba (2.1e17 J), Krakatoa 1883 (8.4e17 J), the Chicxulub impact (4.2e23 J), the Sun's output for a second (3.8e26 J) and Earth's gravitational binding energy (2.49e32 J). The page names the nearest rung below and a multiple, so it says things like "300 hand grenades". The new rule: a comparison never shows a multiple above about 10x or a share below about 10%, so the ladder needs a rung at least every factor of about 10 (100x at the very most), from about 1 J (the gentlest efforts on the page) to beyond a supernova (the page's energies reach above 1e40 J at the top of its strength dial). One shared ladder, a mix of kinds of event. Existing facts for the current rungs are in /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/research/final-environment.json (keys energy_*), final-humans.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass) and final-objects.json (toyota_corolla_curb_mass): read them so you don't duplicate keys, and reuse their values where they are right.
What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. Give each one a short page phrase that fits "about 3x ___" and "40% of ___" (for example "a lightning bolt", "the Beirut port explosion of 2020"). Kinetic energies computed from a mass and speed are fine (status derived) if the mass and speed are sourced. Avoid jargon; avoid anything grisly or that a general reader would find tasteless as a yardstick beyond the bombs and disasters the page already uses.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first. A number is "verified" only if you fetched the page or PDF yourself and saw the number there; give the exact URL you fetched. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Where the literature gives a range, record low_si and high_si and the value used, and say why that value (the asteroid's existing fact is the model). Note how uncertain each value is: the page gives only a rough multiple ("roughly 3x") for a reference uncertain by more than about 2x either way.

What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. A number is "verified" only if you fetched the page or PDF yourself and saw the number there; give the exact URL you fetched. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Project: the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a one-page physics simulator for Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). Read section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)") before anything else: it is the task. Today the page compares every energy to a ladder of eleven references (build-data.py, the 'energy' list; app.html compareEnergy): the fastest pitch (162 J), a Corolla at 100 km/h (0.52 MJ), an M67 hand grenade (1.0 MJ), the MOAB (4.6e10 J), Hiroshima (6.3e13 J), Castle Bravo (6.3e16 J), the Tsar Bomba (2.1e17 J), Krakatoa 1883 (8.4e17 J), the Chicxulub impact (4.2e23 J), the Sun's output for a second (3.8e26 J) and Earth's gravitational binding energy (2.49e32 J). The page names the nearest rung below and a multiple, so it says things like "300 hand grenades". The new rule: a comparison never shows a multiple above about 10x or a share below about 10%, so the ladder needs a rung at least every factor of about 10 (100x at the very most), from about 1 J (the gentlest efforts on the page) to beyond a supernova (the page's energies reach above 1e40 J at the top of its strength dial). One shared ladder, a mix of kinds of event. Existing facts for the current rungs are in /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/research/final-environment.json (keys energy_*), final-humans.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass) and final-objects.json (toyota_corolla_curb_mass): read them so you don't duplicate keys, and reuse their values where they are right.
What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. Give each one a short page phrase that fits "about 3x ___" and "40% of ___" (for example "a lightning bolt", "the Beirut port explosion of 2020"). Kinetic energies computed from a mass and speed are fine (status derived) if the mass and speed are sourced. Avoid jargon; avoid anything grisly or that a general reader would find tasteless as a yardstick beyond the bombs and disasters the page already uses.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first. A number is "verified" only if you fetched the page or PDF yourself and saw the number there; give the exact URL you fetched. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Where the literature gives a range, record low_si and high_si and the value used, and say why that value (the asteroid's existing fact is the model). Note how uncertain each value is: the page gives only a rough multiple ("roughly 3x") for a reference uncertain by more than about 2x either way.
Load web tools with ToolSearch query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch". For PDFs, curl them into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ and extract text with python (pip install --user pypdf if needed) or pdftotext. Keep raw downloads and scripts under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ (create it). Do not edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab.
Fact fields (the lab's research format): key (snake_case, prefix energy_, e.g. energy_lightning_bolt), category ("energy_reference"), label, status (verified = number seen in a fetched primary or authoritative source | derived = computed by you from verified inputs, formula and inputs in notes | estimate = a reasoned assumption | reported = secondary or weak source only | disputed = sources disagree materially), value_si (J, a number), unit_si ("J"), low_si and high_si when there is a range, display (short human text with the original units, e.g. "about 1 GJ per flash (NOAA: typical 1-10 GJ)"), sources (title + exact URL fetched), notes (exact quote or table cell, conditions, caveats; under about 900 characters), who_when, and page_short (the short phrase for the page). For a derived kinetic energy, also give the input facts (mass, speed) as their own facts.

TOPIC "geophysical": rungs from about 1e17 J to about 1e26 J, filling the Krakatoa (8.4e17) to Chicxulub (4.2e23) gap (500,000x) and Chicxulub to the Sun's output for a second (3.8e26 J, 900x). Candidates (unverified): Tambora 1815 (volcanology papers; a range), the 2004 Sumatra-Andaman and 2011 Tohoku earthquakes (USGS radiated energy, e.g. 1.1e18 J and 1.9e17 J; also the total energy if a source gives it; say which), a hurricane's energy per day (NOAA AOML Hurricane FAQ: heat released by cloud formation about 5.2e19 J per day; kinetic energy of the winds about 1.3e17 J per day), a year of all human energy use (the IEA World Energy Outlook or Energy Institute Statistical Review: total primary energy supply, about 600 EJ in recent years; give the year), a day and a year of sunlight reaching Earth (derived: total solar irradiance about 1361 W/m^2 from Kopp & Lean 2011 or the IAU/NASA, times pi R_E^2 times the time), the energy of a large impact such as the one that made the Vredefort or Sudbury crater (journal estimates; ranges), the Toba super-eruption, the yearly geothermal heat flow out of Earth (about 47 TW, Davies & Davies 2010: about 1.5e21 J per year), the Earth's total yearly earthquake energy. Pick about one per decade.

Project: the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a one-page physics simulator for Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). Today the page compares every energy to a ladder of eleven references (build-data.py, the 'energy' list; app.html compareEnergy): the fastest pitch (162 J), a Corolla at 100 km/h (0.52 MJ), an M67 hand grenade (1.0 MJ), the MOAB (4.6e10 J), Hiroshima (6.3e13 J), Castle Bravo (6.3e16 J), the Tsar Bomba (2.1e17 J), Krakatoa 1883 (8.4e17 J), the Chicxulub impact (4.2e23 J), the Sun's output for a second (3.8e26 J) and Earth's gravitational binding energy (2.49e32 J). The page names the nearest rung below and a multiple, so it says things like "300 hand grenades". The new rule: a comparison never shows a multiple above about 10x or a share below about 10%, so the ladder needs a rung at least every factor of about 10 (100x at the very most), from about 1 J (the gentlest efforts on the page) to beyond a supernova (the page's energies reach above 1e40 J at the top of its strength dial). One shared ladder, a mix of kinds of event. Existing facts for the current rungs are in /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/research/final-environment.json (keys energy_*), final-humans.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass) and final-objects.json (toyota_corolla_curb_mass): read them so you don't duplicate keys, and reuse their values where they are right.
What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. Give each one a short page phrase that fits "about 3x ___" and "40% of ___" (for example "a lightning bolt", "the Beirut port explosion of 2020"). Kinetic energies computed from a mass and speed are fine (status derived) if the mass and speed are sourced. Avoid jargon; avoid anything grisly or that a general reader would find tasteless as a yardstick beyond the bombs and disasters the page already uses.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first. A number is "verified" only if you fetched the page or PDF yourself and saw the number there; give the exact URL you fetched. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Where the literature gives a range, record low_si and high_si and the value used, and say why that value (the asteroid's existing fact is the model). Note how uncertain each value is: the page gives only a rough multiple ("roughly 3x") for a reference uncertain by more than about 2x either way.
Load web tools with ToolSearch query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch". For PDFs, curl them into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ and extract text with python (pip install --user pypdf if needed) or pdftotext. Keep raw downloads and scripts under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ (create it). Fact fields (the lab's research format): key (snake_case, prefix energy_, e.g. energy_lightning_bolt), category ("energy_reference"), label, status (verified = number seen in a fetched primary or authoritative source | derived = computed by you from verified inputs, formula and inputs in notes | estimate = a reasoned assumption | reported = secondary or weak source only | disputed = sources disagree materially), value_si (J, a number), unit_si ("J"), low_si and high_si when there is a range, display (short human text with the original units, e.g. "about 1 GJ per flash (NOAA: typical 1-10 GJ)"), sources (title + exact URL fetched), notes (exact quote or table cell, conditions, caveats; under about 900 characters), who_when, and page_short (the short phrase for the page). For a derived kinetic energy, also give the input facts (mass, speed) as their own facts.

You are the skeptical fact-checker for topic "geophysical". Below are the researcher's facts and proposed rungs. Fetch EVERY cited source for EVERY fact yourself (list the URLs you fetched in each check), and check each value, unit conversion, range, quotation, date and status against what the source actually says; recompute every derived number with your own script. Mark ok=false with a correction for anything wrong or mislabelled: a number not on the cited page, a secondary summary presented as the primary source, a weak source marked verified, a range collapsed to a point, a wrong unit or TNT conversion (1 t TNT = 4.184e9 J exactly), an uncertainty understated. Project: the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a one-page physics simulator for Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). Read section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)") before anything else: it is the task. Project: the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a one-page physics simulator for Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). Read section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)") before anything else: it is the task. Today the page compares every energy to a ladder of eleven references (build-data.py, the 'energy' list; app.html compareEnergy): the fastest pitch (162 J), a Corolla at 100 km/h (0.52 MJ), an M67 hand grenade (1.0 MJ), the MOAB (4.6e10 J), Hiroshima (6.3e13 J), Castle Bravo (6.3e16 J), the Tsar Bomba (2.1e17 J), Krakatoa 1883 (8.4e17 J), the Chicxulub impact (4.2e23 J), the Sun's output for a second (3.8e26 J) and Earth's gravitational binding energy (2.49e32 J). The page names the nearest rung below and a multiple, so it says things like "300 hand grenades". The new rule: a comparison never shows a multiple above about 10x or a share below about 10%, so the ladder needs a rung at least every factor of about 10 (100x at the very most), from about 1 J (the gentlest efforts on the page) to beyond a supernova (the page's energies reach above 1e40 J at the top of its strength dial). One shared ladder, a mix of kinds of event. Existing facts for the current rungs are in /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/research/final-environment.json (keys energy_*), final-humans.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass) and final-objects.json (toyota_corolla_curb_mass): read them so you don't duplicate keys, and reuse their values where they are right.
What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. Give each one a short page phrase that fits "about 3x ___" and "40% of ___" (for example "a lightning bolt", "the Beirut port explosion of 2020"). Kinetic energies computed from a mass and speed are fine (status derived) if the mass and speed are sourced. Avoid jargon; avoid anything grisly or that a general reader would find tasteless as a yardstick beyond the bombs and disasters the page already uses.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first. A number is "verified" only if you fetched the page or PDF yourself and saw the number there; give the exact URL you fetched. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Where the literature gives a range, record low_si and high_si and the value used, and say why that value (the asteroid's existing fact is the model). What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Where the literature gives a range, record low_si and high_si and the value used, and say why that value (the asteroid's existing fact is the model). Note how uncertain each value is: the page gives only a rough multiple ("roughly 3x") for a reference uncertain by more than about 2x either way.

For a derived kinetic energy, also give the input facts (mass, speed) as their own facts.

TOPIC "audit": the existing rungs, against the same standard ("Also check, while researching: the existing rungs' values and sources"). For each current rung, re-fetch its sources and try hard to find a better one (primary or authoritative), then give the corrected fact (same key) with an honest status. In particular: the fastest pitch on record (Aroldis Chapman, 105.8 mph, 2010: MLB Statcast or MLB.com; baseball mass from the MLB Official Baseball Rules 3.01: 5 to 5.25 oz); the Corolla's curb mass (Toyota's own spec sheet); the M67 grenade (US Army TC 3-23.30 for the 6.5 oz Composition B fill; a better source than Wikipedia for Comp B's energy, e.g. a detonation-energy or heat-of-detonation figure from a US Army or DoD handbook, LLNL Explosives Handbook, or a journal; the brief allows a range); the MOAB (US Air Force or DoD statements, GlobalSecurity, AFRL; 11 t TNT); Hiroshima (LANL LA-8819, Malik 1985; DOE/OSTI; the Radiation Effects Research Foundation DS02 report gives 16 kt); Castle Bravo (DOE/NV-209 United States Nuclear Tests, on osti.gov or nnss.gov; 15 Mt); the Tsar Bomba (Rosatom, Russian sources, Sublette's archive; 50 Mt); Krakatoa 1883 (a volcanology paper or the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Self & Rampino 1981, Simkin & Fiske 1983; the energy figure is soft); Chicxulub (journal papers; keep a range); the Sun's luminosity (IAU 2015 B3, verified); Earth's binding energy (a textbook or paper, or our PREM integral fact energy_earth_binding_prem_computed in final-density.json). Propose replacements where a rung is too weak or obscure, and keep each fact's key.

Project: the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a one-page physics simulator for Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). Read section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)") before anything else: it is the task. Today the page compares every energy to a ladder of eleven references (build-data.py, the 'energy' list; app.html compareEnergy): the fastest pitch (162 J), a Corolla at 100 km/h (0.52 MJ), an M67 hand grenade (1.0 MJ), the MOAB (4.6e10 J), Hiroshima (6.3e13 J), Castle Bravo (6.3e16 J), the Tsar Bomba (2.1e17 J), Krakatoa 1883 (8.4e17 J), the Chicxulub impact (4.2e23 J), the Sun's output for a second (3.8e26 J) and Earth's gravitational binding energy (2.49e32 J). The page names the nearest rung below and a multiple, so it says things like "300 hand grenades". The new rule: a comparison never shows a multiple above about 10x or a share below about 10%, so the ladder needs a rung at least every factor of about 10 (100x at the very most), from about 1 J (the gentlest efforts on the page) to beyond a supernova (the page's energies reach above 1e40 J at the top of its strength dial). One shared ladder, a mix of kinds of event. Existing facts for the current rungs are in /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/research/final-environment.json (keys energy_*), final-humans.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass) and final-objects.json (toyota_corolla_curb_mass): read them so you don't duplicate keys, and reuse their values where they are right.
What makes a good rung: something a general reader can picture or has heard of (a rifle bullet, a lightning bolt, a train at full speed, the Beirut explosion, a hurricane, a year of all human energy use, the Moon), with a well-sourced energy. Prefer events and objects with a single clear number. Give each one a short page phrase that fits "about 3x ___" and "40% of ___" (for example "a lightning bolt", "the Beirut port explosion of 2020"). Kinetic energies computed from a mass and speed are fine (status derived) if the mass and speed are sourced. Avoid jargon; avoid anything grisly or that a general reader would find tasteless as a yardstick beyond the bombs and disasters the page already uses.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first. A number is "verified" only if you fetched the page or PDF yourself and saw the number there; give the exact URL you fetched. Prefer primary or authoritative sources: journals (DOI landing pages, PubMed, publisher PDFs, arXiv for astrophysics with the published version noted), government agencies and labs (USGS, NASA, NOAA, NWS, DOE, LANL, Sandia, NIST, IAEA, IEA, EIA, ESA), standards bodies, textbooks, manufacturers' and armed forces' published specifications. Wikipedia and news only when nothing better exists; then the status is "reported" and you say so. Where the literature gives a range, record low_si and high_si and the value used, and say why that value (the asteroid's existing fact is the model). Note how uncertain each value is: the page gives only a rough multiple ("roughly 3x") for a reference uncertain by more than about 2x either way.
Load web tools with ToolSearch query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch". For PDFs, curl them into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ and extract text with python (pip install --user pypdf if needed) or pdftotext. Keep raw downloads and scripts under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/researchC/<topic>/ (create it). Do not edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab.
Fact fields (the lab's research format): key (snake_case, prefix energy_, e.g. energy_lightning_bolt), category ("energy_reference"), label, status (verified = number seen in a fetched primary or authoritative source | derived = computed by you from verified inputs, formula and inputs in notes | estimate = a reasoned assumption | reported = secondary or weak source only | disputed = sources disagree materially), value_si (J, a number), unit_si ("J"), low_si and high_si when there is a range, display (short human text with the original units, e.g. "about 1 GJ per flash (NOAA: typical 1-10 GJ)"), sources (title + exact URL fetched), notes (exact quote or table cell, conditions, caveats; under about 900 characters), who_when, and page_short (the short phrase for the page). For a derived kinetic energy, also give the input facts (mass, speed) as their own facts.

You are the skeptical fact-checker for topic "small". Below are the researcher's facts and proposed rungs. Fetch EVERY cited source for EVERY fact yourself (list the URLs you fetched in each check), and check each value, unit conversion, range, quotation, date and status against what the source actually says; recompute every derived number with your own script. Mark ok=false with a correction for anything wrong or mislabelled: a number not on the cited page, a secondary summary presented as the primary source, a weak source marked verified, a range collapsed to a point, a wrong unit or TNT conversion (1 t TNT = 4.184e9 J exactly), an uncertainty understated. If a source can't be fetched, say so and downgrade the status unless another fetched source confirms the number. Also judge the proposed rungs as page yardsticks (plain, picturable, not misleading) and list decades in the band still without a rung within 10x. Do not edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab.

args.prompt:
You are reviewing a change to the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a self-contained HTML page (a claude.ai Artifact) that simulates Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). The change is on branch claude/rex-gui-c and implements section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)"; read "Rules for every item" and section 6 first). In short: every energy on the page is compared with a ladder of reference energies ("Compared with" tiles on Punch, Clap, Stomp; the Weight tab's energy tile; the game of catch and Collide texts). The old ladder had eleven rungs; the new one has 58, from the energy to lift a 100 g apple one metre (0.99 J) to GW150914 (5.4e47 J). The wording is in src/ladder.js (compare, gaps): the nearest rung on a log scale; a multiple of the rung below (at most about 10x) or a share of the rung above (at least about 10%); 'about the same as' within 15%; rough rungs (fact range more than 2x from the value, or the fact's field rough with a reason) get 1 figure and 'roughly'; past either end 'beyond the ladder'. The rungs are picked in build-data.py (LADDER; each rung is one research fact, its energy the fact's value_si and its phrase the fact's page_short; a sources-table row per rung). The facts are in research/final-energy.json (140 facts), merged from seven researched topics, each checked by a skeptic who fetched every source; the research record with every skeptic check and the merge decisions is research/reviews/gui-c-research.json. Three facts were updated in place in final-humans.json and final-objects.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass, toyota_corolla_curb_mass); twelve old energy facts moved from final-environment.json to final-energy.json. The page also gained an 'Energy comparisons' card (src/static-data.js), new growth what-if notes for Krakatoa and the dinosaur-killer (app.html growthWhatIf, 'firm'), and new tests: test/ladder.js (the brief's tests) and a block in test/shots.js.
See the diff: git -C /home/user/rex-strength-lab diff main...claude/rex-gui-c (main's page: git show main:rex-strength-lab/dist/index.html). Build: cd /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab && python3 build-data.py && node build.js. Tests: node test/ladder.js (seconds), node test/calibration.js (80 s), node test/presence.js (60 s), node test/shots.js (5 min; writes dist/preview.html and shots/), node test/powers.js (3 min). In Node: global.window = {}; require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/data.js'); const D = window.DINO_DATA; const L = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/ladder.js'); L.compare(J, D.energyRefs) returns {kind, ref, x, text}. Engine: const P = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js'). For a browser, Playwright and Chromium are in /opt (see test/shots.js for how it finds them); the page keeps its settings in localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' (e.g. {action:'punch', logKg: 20, mode:'comic'}).
The author's recorded decisions (check whether each is justified and stated where the owner will see it; do not report a decision as a defect just because it departs from the brief's letter, unless it is wrong or unjustified):
1. Display rule: src/ladder.js names the nearest rung on a log scale. Above it the page gives a multiple (2 figures), below it a share (2 figures). Rungs are never more than 100x apart (build-data.py asserts it), so the multiple is at most 10x and the share at least 10%. Within 15% of a firm rung: 'about the same as'. A rough rung gets 1 figure and 'roughly', and 'roughly the same as' within 1.5x. Past either end: 'beyond the ladder', naming the end rung, with no number. Energies within the 'same' band just outside an end rung still count as on the ladder.
2. Rough rungs: A rung is rough when its fact's range runs more than 2x from its value (lightning, Beirut, Chicxulub, the nova, the magnetar flare, supernova light, SN 1998bw), or when the fact says so with its reason (field rough): Krakatoa (its own range is the one refereed estimate, but published figures span about 60x) and an average hurricane's heat (an illustrative figure with no stated range; storms differ by a factor of a few). The supernova blast's typical range is exactly 2x, so it stays firm.
3. Grenade: Comp B Grade A: The explosive topic said LLNL's handbook has no measured heat of detonation for Comp B Grade A and used Comp B-3 instead (0.89 MJ). The audit cited the 1981 edition (UCRL-52997, OSTI 6530310), Table 5-2, p. 5-7. Checked on the page image (PDF p. 56): 'Comp B, Grade A', experimental, H2O(l): 1.20 kcal/g (5.02 MJ/kg), 25 C, 8.47 mm charge, density 1.69. The audit is right: the grenade is 0.184 kg x 5.02 MJ/kg = 0.925 MJ. The explosive topic's grenade and Comp B-3 facts are dropped.
4. Duplicates across topics: Hiroshima, Castle Bravo and Earth's binding energy: the audit's versions (Earth's integrates the original PREM paper; the planetary one used a code transcription of it). Facts shared by the planetary and stellar topics (Jupiter's mass and orbital speed, Earth's orbital speed and motion, the Sun's year and century): the planetary versions; they differ from the stellar ones by under 0.1%. Small's pitch and Corolla facts duplicate the audit's: the audit's keys are kept.
5. Facts kept in their own files: fastest_baseball_pitch (final-humans.json), baseball_mass and toyota_corolla_curb_mass (final-objects.json) are updated in place with the audit's versions, keeping their categories. The twelve old energy facts move from final-environment.json to final-energy.json in the audit's versions. Tunguska and the xkcd baseball stay in final-environment.json, unchanged (not rungs). build-data.py now fails if a key is in two research files.
6. Pitch wording: The audit found that 'at release' is our inference for Chapman's 2010 pitch (MLB lists 105.8 mph; Statcast measures at release, but this pitch was tracked by PITCHf/x). The Fastest pitch card now says '47.3 m/s, the ball speed MLB lists. The lab takes it as the speed leaving the hand.'
7. Rung choice: 58 rungs from the energy to lift a 100 g apple one metre (0.99 J) to GW150914 (5.4e47 J). Widest steps: a year of sunlight to the Sun's second (70x), Hiroshima to Chelyabinsk (33x), a day of sunlight to Chicxulub (33x), a day of world energy use to a hurricane's day (28x). Left out as redundant (within 2x of a kept rung, or covering a decade already covered): badminton, the 9 mm and .50-calibre bullets, a Corolla at 50 km/h, Tianjin (Beirut kept: better known), Halifax (the ISS kept: within 4%, better constrained), the Sedan test (obscure), a magnitude-7 quake (an estimate), Mount St Helens, Tunguska, the two earthquakes, a hurricane's wind, Tambora (a magazine figure), Earth's internal heat, Vredefort, the 2003 solar flare, the Sun's minute, the Moon's binding energy, the Moon-forming impact, Saturn's motion, Jupiter's binding energy, the Sun's million years and GW190521. SN 1998bw is kept, rough, because without it the step from Jupiter's mass-energy to a supernova's total energy is 176x.
8. Top of the ladder: The page can show energies far past 1e34 J (the Weight tab takes any mass), so the ladder runs to the first black-hole collision detected (5.4e47 J); above that the page says the energy is beyond the ladder.
9. Growth what-if: Krakatoa and the dinosaur-killer use the ladder's values: 125 Mt (5.2e17 J, the middle of the one refereed estimate) instead of the popular 200 Mt, and 5e23 J (Morgan et al. 2022) instead of the brief's 4.2e23 J. The notes under the what-if say so. The engine tests that use 8.4e17 and 4.2e23 J pass those numbers in directly and are unchanged.
10. Saved-state comparisons: test/shots.js compares saved states with main's page before the reorganisation; the energy comparisons (old and new wording) are set aside there, since section 6 rewrote them.
11. Tests: the brief's three tests are in test/ladder.js (a new file, added to the build line in CLAUDE.md and CI in the pull request), plus a page check in test/shots.js.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first (see CLAUDE.md: every number sourced or labelled an estimate; 'sourced' means fetched and seen on the page, with the exact URL; primary sources preferred; plain numbers and plain words). Do NOT edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab and do not commit; work on copies. Write scratch scripts, downloads and screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewC1/ (create it; use a subfolder named for your lens). Every finding must be reproduced: give the exact input, place or URL, what the page, code or source says (quote it, or the script output), what is correct and why, and a minimal fix. Report real defects only: wrong numbers, numbers not on the cited page, wrong unit conversions or arithmetic, a status that overstates the evidence, a range that hides a wider published spread (which would wrongly make a rung firm), a page phrase that misleads or names the wrong thing, behaviour the brief requires that is missing or wrong, a test that passes when it should not, broken pages (NaN, overflow at 390 px, console errors), contradictions between the page, README and research. Skip style preferences.

LENS: BRIEF COMPLIANCE. Go through BRIEF-gui.md section 6 line by line: the display rule (never a multiple above about 10x or a share below about 10%; test every decade between the bottom and top rungs; uncertain by more than about 2x gets only a rough multiple, generalising the old asteroid special case; plain words, 'about 1.5x a lightning bolt' not 'lightning-bolt equivalents'); the candidate rungs (each dropped one: is the reason sound and recorded?); the gaps the brief names (MOAB to Beirut, Sun-second to the Moon, the Moon to Earth, the Sun's year to a supernova) and both ends' rule (below the bottom rung and above the top one, the energy alone and 'beyond the ladder'); one shared ladder; 'also check the existing rungs' (were all eleven re-checked against the standard?); the full research process (each new reference researched, checked by a skeptic who fetches the source, compiled as a fact with key, status, sources, notes; primary sources preferred; ranges recorded with the value used); the three tests (do test/ladder.js and the shots.js block really test what the brief says, or could they pass on a broken ladder?); 'Rules for every item' (saved pages still load; the brief's tests; every number sourced or labelled; README and Known limits; review records). Check every place the old ladder's ids are used (growth what-if GROW_WHAT, thresholdDefs E(id), any hard-coded text that quotes an old value such as 8.4e17, 4.2e23, 1.0 MJ, '200 Mt') still works and says the right thing. Check section 6's 'changes only the research data and the page's comparison wording' (no engine physics change): diff src/engine.js.

Under verified_ok, list what you checked and found correct (for the source lenses: each rung and the URLs you fetched for it). Prefix finding ids with "brief-".

You are reviewing a change to the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a self-contained HTML page (a claude.ai Artifact) that simulates Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). The change is on branch claude/rex-gui-c and implements section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)"; read "Rules for every item" and section 6 first). In short: every energy on the page is compared with a ladder of reference energies ("Compared with" tiles on Punch, Clap, Stomp; the Weight tab's energy tile; the game of catch and Collide texts). The old ladder had eleven rungs; the new one has 58, from the energy to lift a 100 g apple one metre (0.99 J) to GW150914 (5.4e47 J). The wording is in src/ladder.js (compare, gaps): the nearest rung on a log scale; a multiple of the rung below (at most about 10x) or a share of the rung above (at least about 10%); 'about the same as' within 15%; rough rungs (fact range more than 2x from the value, or the fact's field rough with a reason) get 1 figure and 'roughly'; past either end 'beyond the ladder'. The rungs are picked in build-data.py (LADDER; each rung is one research fact, its energy the fact's value_si and its phrase the fact's page_short; a sources-table row per rung). The facts are in research/final-energy.json (140 facts), merged from seven researched topics, each checked by a skeptic who fetched every source; the research record with every skeptic check and the merge decisions is research/reviews/gui-c-research.json. Three facts were updated in place in final-humans.json and final-objects.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass, toyota_corolla_curb_mass); twelve old energy facts moved from final-environment.json to final-energy.json. The page also gained an 'Energy comparisons' card (src/static-data.js), new growth what-if notes for Krakatoa and the dinosaur-killer (app.html growthWhatIf, 'firm'), and new tests: test/ladder.js (the brief's tests) and a block in test/shots.js.
See the diff: git -C /home/user/rex-strength-lab diff main...claude/rex-gui-c (main's page: git show main:rex-strength-lab/dist/index.html). Build: cd /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab && python3 build-data.py && node build.js. Tests: node test/ladder.js (seconds), node test/calibration.js (80 s), node test/presence.js (60 s), node test/shots.js (5 min; writes dist/preview.html and shots/), node test/powers.js (3 min). In Node: global.window = {}; require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/data.js'); const D = window.DINO_DATA; const L = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/ladder.js'); L.compare(J, D.energyRefs) returns {kind, ref, x, text}. Engine: const P = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js'). For a browser, Playwright and Chromium are in /opt (see test/shots.js for how it finds them); the page keeps its settings in localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' (e.g. {action:'punch', logKg: 20, mode:'comic'}).
The author's recorded decisions (check whether each is justified and stated where the owner will see it; do not report a decision as a defect just because it departs from the brief's letter, unless it is wrong or unjustified):
1. Display rule: src/ladder.js names the nearest rung on a log scale. Above it the page gives a multiple (2 figures), below it a share (2 figures). Rungs are never more than 100x apart (build-data.py asserts it), so the multiple is at most 10x and the share at least 10%. Within 15% of a firm rung: 'about the same as'. A rough rung gets 1 figure and 'roughly', and 'roughly the same as' within 1.5x. Past either end: 'beyond the ladder', naming the end rung, with no number. Energies within the 'same' band just outside an end rung still count as on the ladder.
2. Rough rungs: A rung is rough when its fact's range runs more than 2x from its value (lightning, Beirut, Chicxulub, the nova, the magnetar flare, supernova light, SN 1998bw), or when the fact says so with its reason (field rough): Krakatoa (its own range is the one refereed estimate, but published figures span about 60x) and an average hurricane's heat (an illustrative figure with no stated range; storms differ by a factor of a few). The supernova blast's typical range is exactly 2x, so it stays firm.
3. Grenade: Comp B Grade A: The explosive topic said LLNL's handbook has no measured heat of detonation for Comp B Grade A and used Comp B-3 instead (0.89 MJ). The audit cited the 1981 edition (UCRL-52997, OSTI 6530310), Table 5-2, p. 5-7. Checked on the page image (PDF p. 56): 'Comp B, Grade A', experimental, H2O(l): 1.20 kcal/g (5.02 MJ/kg), 25 C, 8.47 mm charge, density 1.69. The audit is right: the grenade is 0.184 kg x 5.02 MJ/kg = 0.925 MJ. The explosive topic's grenade and Comp B-3 facts are dropped.
4. Duplicates across topics: Hiroshima, Castle Bravo and Earth's binding energy: the audit's versions (Earth's integrates the original PREM paper; the planetary one used a code transcription of it). Facts shared by the planetary and stellar topics (Jupiter's mass and orbital speed, Earth's orbital speed and motion, the Sun's year and century): the planetary versions; they differ from the stellar ones by under 0.1%. Small's pitch and Corolla facts duplicate the audit's: the audit's keys are kept.
5. Facts kept in their own files: fastest_baseball_pitch (final-humans.json), baseball_mass and toyota_corolla_curb_mass (final-objects.json) are updated in place with the audit's versions, keeping their categories. The twelve old energy facts move from final-environment.json to final-energy.json in the audit's versions. Tunguska and the xkcd baseball stay in final-environment.json, unchanged (not rungs). build-data.py now fails if a key is in two research files.
6. Pitch wording: The audit found that 'at release' is our inference for Chapman's 2010 pitch (MLB lists 105.8 mph; Statcast measures at release, but this pitch was tracked by PITCHf/x). The Fastest pitch card now says '47.3 m/s, the ball speed MLB lists. The lab takes it as the speed leaving the hand.'
7. Rung choice: 58 rungs from the energy to lift a 100 g apple one metre (0.99 J) to GW150914 (5.4e47 J). Widest steps: a year of sunlight to the Sun's second (70x), Hiroshima to Chelyabinsk (33x), a day of sunlight to Chicxulub (33x), a day of world energy use to a hurricane's day (28x). Left out as redundant (within 2x of a kept rung, or covering a decade already covered): badminton, the 9 mm and .50-calibre bullets, a Corolla at 50 km/h, Tianjin (Beirut kept: better known), Halifax (the ISS kept: within 4%, better constrained), the Sedan test (obscure), a magnitude-7 quake (an estimate), Mount St Helens, Tunguska, the two earthquakes, a hurricane's wind, Tambora (a magazine figure), Earth's internal heat, Vredefort, the 2003 solar flare, the Sun's minute, the Moon's binding energy, the Moon-forming impact, Saturn's motion, Jupiter's binding energy, the Sun's million years and GW190521. SN 1998bw is kept, rough, because without it the step from Jupiter's mass-energy to a supernova's total energy is 176x.
8. Top of the ladder: The page can show energies far past 1e34 J (the Weight tab takes any mass), so the ladder runs to the first black-hole collision detected (5.4e47 J); above that the page says the energy is beyond the ladder.
9. Growth what-if: Krakatoa and the dinosaur-killer use the ladder's values: 125 Mt (5.2e17 J, the middle of the one refereed estimate) instead of the popular 200 Mt, and 5e23 J (Morgan et al. 2022) instead of the brief's 4.2e23 J. The notes under the what-if say so. The engine tests that use 8.4e17 and 4.2e23 J pass those numbers in directly and are unchanged.
10. Saved-state comparisons: test/shots.js compares saved states with main's page before the reorganisation; the energy comparisons (old and new wording) are set aside there, since section 6 rewrote them.
11. Tests: the brief's three tests are in test/ladder.js (a new file, added to the build line in CLAUDE.md and CI in the pull request), plus a page check in test/shots.js.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first (see CLAUDE.md: every number sourced or labelled an estimate; 'sourced' means fetched and seen on the page, with the exact URL; primary sources preferred; plain numbers and plain words). Do NOT edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab and do not commit; work on copies. Write scratch scripts, downloads and screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewC1/ (create it; use a subfolder named for your lens). Every finding must be reproduced: give the exact input, place or URL, what the page, code or source says (quote it, or the script output), what is correct and why, and a minimal fix. Report real defects only: wrong numbers, numbers not on the cited page, wrong unit conversions or arithmetic, a status that overstates the evidence, a range that hides a wider published spread (which would wrongly make a rung firm), a page phrase that misleads or names the wrong thing, behaviour the brief requires that is missing or wrong, a test that passes when it should not, broken pages (NaN, overflow at 390 px, console errors), contradictions between the page, README and research. Skip style preferences.

Another reviewer (srclow lens) reported the findings below. For EACH one, try hard to REFUTE it: reproduce it yourself with your own script, browser run or fetch of the source, independently of theirs (write it under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewC1/verify-srclow/). Mark real=true only if you reproduced it; put the command or URL and its output or quote in reproduction. Confirm the severity and give the best minimal fix (exact code, text or number). Default to real=false if you cannot reproduce it.

args.prompt:
You are reviewing a change to the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a self-contained HTML page (a claude.ai Artifact) that simulates Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). The change is on branch claude/rex-gui-c and implements section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)"; read "Rules for every item" and section 6 first). In short: every energy on the page is compared with a ladder of reference energies ("Compared with" tiles on Punch, Clap, Stomp; the Weight tab's energy tile; the game of catch and Collide texts). The old ladder had eleven rungs; the new one has 58, from the energy to lift a 100 g apple one metre (0.99 J) to GW150914 (5.4e47 J). The wording is in src/ladder.js (compare, gaps): the nearest rung on a log scale; a multiple of the rung below (at most about 10x) or a share of the rung above (at least about 10%); 'about the same as' within 15%; rough rungs (fact range more than 2x from the value, or the fact's field rough with a reason) get 1 figure and 'roughly'; past either end 'beyond the ladder'. The rungs are picked in build-data.py (LADDER; each rung is one research fact, its energy the fact's value_si and its phrase the fact's page_short; a sources-table row per rung). The facts are in research/final-energy.json (140 facts), merged from seven researched topics, each checked by a skeptic who fetched every source; the research record with every skeptic check and the merge decisions is research/reviews/gui-c-research.json. Three facts were updated in place in final-humans.json and final-objects.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass, toyota_corolla_curb_mass); twelve old energy facts moved from final-environment.json to final-energy.json. The page also gained an 'Energy comparisons' card (src/static-data.js), new growth what-if notes for Krakatoa and the dinosaur-killer (app.html growthWhatIf, 'firm'), and new tests: test/ladder.js (the brief's tests) and a block in test/shots.js.
See the diff: git -C /home/user/rex-strength-lab diff main...claude/rex-gui-c (main's page: git show main:rex-strength-lab/dist/index.html). Build: cd /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab && python3 build-data.py && node build.js. Tests: node test/ladder.js (seconds), node test/calibration.js (80 s), node test/presence.js (60 s), node test/shots.js (5 min; writes dist/preview.html and shots/), node test/powers.js (3 min). In Node: global.window = {}; require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/data.js'); const D = window.DINO_DATA; const L = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/ladder.js'); L.compare(J, D.energyRefs) returns {kind, ref, x, text}. Engine: const P = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js'). For a browser, Playwright and Chromium are in /opt (see test/shots.js for how it finds them); the page keeps its settings in localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' (e.g. {action:'punch', logKg: 20, mode:'comic'}).
The author's recorded decisions (check whether each is justified and stated where the owner will see it; do not report a decision as a defect just because it departs from the brief's letter, unless it is wrong or unjustified):
1. Display rule: src/ladder.js names the nearest rung on a log scale. Above it the page gives a multiple (2 figures), below it a share (2 figures). Rungs are never more than 100x apart (build-data.py asserts it), so the multiple is at most 10x and the share at least 10%. Within 15% of a firm rung: 'about the same as'. A rough rung gets 1 figure and 'roughly', and 'roughly the same as' within 1.5x. Past either end: 'beyond the ladder', naming the end rung, with no number. Energies within the 'same' band just outside an end rung still count as on the ladder.
2. Rough rungs: A rung is rough when its fact's range runs more than 2x from its value (lightning, Beirut, Chicxulub, the nova, the magnetar flare, supernova light, SN 1998bw), or when the fact says so with its reason (field rough): Krakatoa (its own range is the one refereed estimate, but published figures span about 60x) and an average hurricane's heat (an illustrative figure with no stated range; storms differ by a factor of a few). The supernova blast's typical range is exactly 2x, so it stays firm.
3. Grenade: Comp B Grade A: The explosive topic said LLNL's handbook has no measured heat of detonation for Comp B Grade A and used Comp B-3 instead (0.89 MJ). The audit cited the 1981 edition (UCRL-52997, OSTI 6530310), Table 5-2, p. 5-7. Checked on the page image (PDF p. 56): 'Comp B, Grade A', experimental, H2O(l): 1.20 kcal/g (5.02 MJ/kg), 25 C, 8.47 mm charge, density 1.69. The audit is right: the grenade is 0.184 kg x 5.02 MJ/kg = 0.925 MJ. The explosive topic's grenade and Comp B-3 facts are dropped.
4. Duplicates across topics: Hiroshima, Castle Bravo and Earth's binding energy: the audit's versions (Earth's integrates the original PREM paper; the planetary one used a code transcription of it). Facts shared by the planetary and stellar topics (Jupiter's mass and orbital speed, Earth's orbital speed and motion, the Sun's year and century): the planetary versions; they differ from the stellar ones by under 0.1%. Small's pitch and Corolla facts duplicate the audit's: the audit's keys are kept.
5. Facts kept in their own files: fastest_baseball_pitch (final-humans.json), baseball_mass and toyota_corolla_curb_mass (final-objects.json) are updated in place with the audit's versions, keeping their categories. The twelve old energy facts move from final-environment.json to final-energy.json in the audit's versions. Tunguska and the xkcd baseball stay in final-environment.json, unchanged (not rungs). build-data.py now fails if a key is in two research files.
6. Pitch wording: The audit found that 'at release' is our inference for Chapman's 2010 pitch (MLB lists 105.8 mph; Statcast measures at release, but this pitch was tracked by PITCHf/x). The Fastest pitch card now says '47.3 m/s, the ball speed MLB lists. The lab takes it as the speed leaving the hand.'
7. Rung choice: 58 rungs from the energy to lift a 100 g apple one metre (0.99 J) to GW150914 (5.4e47 J). Widest steps: a year of sunlight to the Sun's second (70x), Hiroshima to Chelyabinsk (33x), a day of sunlight to Chicxulub (33x), a day of world energy use to a hurricane's day (28x). Left out as redundant (within 2x of a kept rung, or covering a decade already covered): badminton, the 9 mm and .50-calibre bullets, a Corolla at 50 km/h, Tianjin (Beirut kept: better known), Halifax (the ISS kept: within 4%, better constrained), the Sedan test (obscure), a magnitude-7 quake (an estimate), Mount St Helens, Tunguska, the two earthquakes, a hurricane's wind, Tambora (a magazine figure), Earth's internal heat, Vredefort, the 2003 solar flare, the Sun's minute, the Moon's binding energy, the Moon-forming impact, Saturn's motion, Jupiter's binding energy, the Sun's million years and GW190521. SN 1998bw is kept, rough, because without it the step from Jupiter's mass-energy to a supernova's total energy is 176x.
8. Top of the ladder: The page can show energies far past 1e34 J (the Weight tab takes any mass), so the ladder runs to the first black-hole collision detected (5.4e47 J); above that the page says the energy is beyond the ladder.
9. Growth what-if: Krakatoa and the dinosaur-killer use the ladder's values: 125 Mt (5.2e17 J, the middle of the one refereed estimate) instead of the popular 200 Mt, and 5e23 J (Morgan et al. 2022) instead of the brief's 4.2e23 J. The notes under the what-if say so. The engine tests that use 8.4e17 and 4.2e23 J pass those numbers in directly and are unchanged.
10. Saved-state comparisons: test/shots.js compares saved states with main's page before the reorganisation; the energy comparisons (old and new wording) are set aside there, since section 6 rewrote them.
11. Tests: the brief's three tests are in test/ladder.js (a new file, added to the build line in CLAUDE.md and CI in the pull request), plus a page check in test/shots.js.
The owner is a professional critic: factual accuracy and honest labelling come first (see CLAUDE.md: every number sourced or labelled an estimate; 'sourced' means fetched and seen on the page, with the exact URL; primary sources preferred; plain numbers and plain words). Do NOT edit anything under /home/user/rex-strength-lab and do not commit; work on copies. Write scratch scripts, downloads and screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewC1/ (create it; use a subfolder named for your lens). Every finding must be reproduced: give the exact input, place or URL, what the page, code or source says (quote it, or the script output), what is correct and why, and a minimal fix. Report real defects only: wrong numbers, numbers not on the cited page, wrong unit conversions or arithmetic, a status that overstates the evidence, a range that hides a wider published spread (which would wrongly make a rung firm), a page phrase that misleads or names the wrong thing, behaviour the brief requires that is missing or wrong, a test that passes when it should not, broken pages (NaN, overflow at 390 px, console errors), contradictions between the page, README and research. Skip style preferences.

Another reviewer (copy lens) reported the findings below. For EACH one, try hard to REFUTE it: reproduce it yourself with your own script, browser run or fetch of the source, independently of theirs (write it under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-rex-strength-lab/70d4d2aa-c3a8-5eb5-9c7c-1c92e3162d09/scratchpad/reviewC1/verify-copy/). Mark real=true only if you reproduced it; put the command or URL and its output or quote in reproduction. Confirm the severity and give the best minimal fix (exact code, text or number). Default to real=false if you cannot reproduce it.

args.prompt:
You are reviewing a change to the Rex Super-Strength Lab (/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/), a self-contained HTML page (a claude.ai Artifact) that simulates Rex and Ollie (canon in CLAUDE.md, already loaded). The change is on branch claude/rex-gui-c and implements section 6 of /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/BRIEF-gui.md ("More points of comparison for energy (research first)"; read "Rules for every item" and section 6 first). In short: every energy on the page is compared with a ladder of reference energies ("Compared with" tiles on Punch, Clap, Stomp; the Weight tab's energy tile; the game of catch and Collide texts). The old ladder had eleven rungs; the new one has 58, from the energy to lift a 100 g apple one metre (0.99 J) to GW150914 (5.4e47 J). The wording is in src/ladder.js (compare, gaps): the nearest rung on a log scale; a multiple of the rung below (at most about 10x) or a share of the rung above (at least about 10%); 'about the same as' within 15%; rough rungs (fact range more than 2x from the value, or the fact's field rough with a reason) get 1 figure and 'roughly'; past either end 'beyond the ladder'. The rungs are picked in build-data.py (LADDER; each rung is one research fact, its energy the fact's value_si and its phrase the fact's page_short; a sources-table row per rung). The facts are in research/final-energy.json (140 facts), merged from seven researched topics, each checked by a skeptic who fetched every source; the research record with every skeptic check and the merge decisions is research/reviews/gui-c-research.json. Three facts were updated in place in final-humans.json and final-objects.json (fastest_baseball_pitch, baseball_mass, toyota_corolla_curb_mass); twelve old energy facts moved from final-environment.json to final-energy.json. The page also gained an 'Energy comparisons' card (src/static-data.js), new growth what-if notes for Krakatoa and the dinosaur-killer (app.html growthWhatIf, 'firm'), and new tests: test/ladder.js (the brief's tests) and a block in test/shots.js.
See the diff: git -C /home/user/rex-strength-lab diff main...claude/rex-gui-c (main's page: git show main:rex-strength-lab/dist/index.html). Build: cd /home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab && python3 build-data.py && node build.js. Tests: node test/ladder.js (seconds), node test/calibration.js (80 s), node test/presence.js (60 s), node test/shots.js (5 min; writes dist/preview.html and shots/), node test/powers.js (3 min). In Node: global.window = {}; require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/data.js'); const D = window.DINO_DATA; const L = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/ladder.js'); L.compare(J, D.energyRefs) returns {kind, ref, x, text}. Engine: const P = require('/home/user/rex-strength-lab/rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js'). For a browser, Playwright and Chromium are in /opt (see test/shots.js for how it finds them); the page keeps its settings in localStorage 'rex-lab-v1' (e.g. {action:'punch', logKg: 20, mode:'comic'}).
The author's recorded decisions (check whether each is justified and stated where the owner will see it; do not report a decision as a defect just because it departs from the brief's letter, unless it is wrong or unjustified):
1. Display rule: src/ladder.js names the nearest rung on a log scale. Above it the page gives a multiple (2 figures), below it a share (2 figures). Rungs are never more than 100x apart (build-data.py asserts it), so the multiple is at most 10x and the share at least 10%. Within 15% of a firm rung: 'about the same as'. A rough rung gets 1 figure and 'roughly', and 'roughly the same as' within 1.5x. Past either end: 'beyond the ladder', naming the end rung, with no number.
